'''RasenBallsport Leipzig e.V.''' ({{Literal translation|Lawn Ball Sports Leipzig}}), commonly known as '''RB Leipzig'''  or informally as '''Red Bull Leipzig,''' or simply '''Leipzig''', is a German professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Leipzig]], Saxony. The club was founded in 2009 by the initiative of the company [[Red Bull GmbH]], which purchased the playing rights of fifth-tier side [[SSV Markranstädt]] with the intent of advancing the new club to the top-flight [[Bundesliga]] within eight years. The men's professional football club is run by the spin-off organization RasenBallsport Leipzig GmbH.<ref name="Impressum">{{cite web |url=http://www.dierotenbullen.com/statisch/impressum.html |title=Impressum |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |website=dierotenbullen.com |location=Leipzig |publisher=RasenBallsport Leipzig GmbH |language=de |access-date= 8 April 2016}}</ref> RB Leipzig plays its home matches at the [[Red Bull Arena (Leipzig)|Red Bull Arena]]. The club nickname is {{langnf|de|Die Roten Bullen|The Red Bulls}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Here's where the Bundesliga clubs' nicknames come from|url=https://bulinews.com/news/386/heres-where-the-bundesliga-clubs-nicknames-come-from|website=Bulinews|date=15 May 2020 |access-date=28 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Football club nicknames: Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, MLS & all team slang terms|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/football-club-nicknames-premier-league-la-liga-serie-a-mls/y258hgejidlw1xede4hbz4ts8|website=Goal (website)|access-date=28 May 2020}}</ref>

After its foundation, RB Leipzig quickly rose through the ranks of German football, starting in the fifth-tier [[NOFV-Oberliga Süd]]. The club achieved successive promotions the following years, eventually being promoted to the Bundesliga in [[2015–16 2. Bundesliga|2015–16]]. In their debut [[2016–17 Bundesliga|top-flight season]], they qualified to the [[UEFA Champions League]] for the first time in their history, following a runner-up finish. They also became a regular feature in the Champions League, reaching the semi-finals of the competition in [[2020 UEFA Champions League Final|2020]]. The club won its first domestic honour, the [[DFB Pokal]], in back-to-back seasons, [[2021–22 DFB-Pokal|2022]] and [[2022–23 DFB-Pokal|2023]].

RB Leipzig's entrance into the upper echelons of German football has proven controversial, as the club's heavy corporate influence is regarded by many Germans to be antithetical to the traditional ownership, structure and management of sports clubs in Germany.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 January 2020 |title=Why RB Leipzig is the most hated team in the Bundesliga |first=Bruce |last=Schoenfeld |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37580461/why-rb-leipzig-most-hated-soccer-team-bundesliga |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On the other hand, some have expressed appreciation for what they view as an honourable endeavour to establish a durable footprint for the Bundesliga in the former [[East Germany]], which previously had been at best tenuous since [[German reunification]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 February 2021 |title=RB Leipzig: Success against Tradition |url=https://www.fournations.football/post/rb-leipzig-success-against-tradition |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=Four Nations}}</ref>

==History==
===2006–2009: Negotiations with various clubs and founding===
Before investing in Leipzig, [[Red Bull GmbH]], led by co-owner [[Dietrich Mateschitz]], spent three and a half years looking for a suitable location to invest in German football.<ref name="Fußballschlaf">{{cite news |last=Flohr |first=Sven |date=13 June 2009 |title=Red Bull reißt Leipzig aus dem Fußballschlaf |trans-title=Red Bull rips Leipzig out of its football sleep|url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article3919661/Red-Bull-reisst-Leipzig-aus-dem-Fussballschlaf.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref> Besides Leipzig, the company also considered a location in [[Old states of Germany|Western Germany]], exploring such cities as [[Hamburg]], [[Munich]] and [[Düsseldorf]].<ref name="PauliKaufen">{{cite news |last=Wöckener |first=Lutz |date=28 April 2015 |title=Red Bull wollte den FC St. Pauli kaufen |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article140232412/Red-Bull-wollte-den-FC-St-Pauli-kaufen.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref>

The company made its first attempt to enter the German football scene in 2006. On the advice of [[Franz Beckenbauer]], a personal friend of Dietrich Mateschitz, the company decided to invest in Leipzig.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport1.at/911+M58e432e9b77.html |title=Leipzig: Red-Bull-Einstieg naht |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=5 December 2012 |website=sport1.at |publisher=Sport1 Multimedia GmbH |location=Wien |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061207020155/http://www.sport1.at/911+M58e432e9b77.html |archive-date=7 December 2006 |access-date=4 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=6 May 2014 |title=Beckenbauer adelt die Bullen aus Leipzig |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/sport/fussball/der-bundesliga-traum-lebt-beckenbauer-adelt-die-bullen-aus-leipzig/9844386.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Handelsblatt]] |location=Düsseldorf |publisher=Handelsblatt GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016 |archive-date=23 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220323051700/https://www.handelsblatt.com/sport/fussball/der-bundesliga-traum-lebt-beckenbauer-adelt-die-bullen-aus-leipzig/9844386.html |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=8 May 2014 |title=Mateschitz nach Attacke gegen RB Leipzig geschockt |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article127772305/Mateschitz-nach-Attacke-gegen-RB-Leipzig-geschockt.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=8 May 2014 |title=Leipzig droht der Lizenzentzug: Red-Bull-Boss attackiert die DFL |url=http://www.n-tv.de/sport/fussball/Red-Bull-Boss-attackiert-die-DFL-article12791216.html |language=de |newspaper=n-tv |location=Cologne |publisher=n-tv Nachrichtenfernsehen GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Machowecz |first=Martin |date=9 May 2014 |title=Wir Ossis brauchen den Retortenverein! |url=http://www.zeit.de/sport/2014-05/fussball-rb-leipzig-zweite-liga-langfassung/seite-2 |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref> The local football club [[FC Sachsen Leipzig]], successor to the former [[List of East German football champions|East German champions]] [[BSG Chemie Leipzig (1950)|BSG Chemie Leipzig]], had for years been in financial difficulties.<ref name="AuflösungSachsen">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=6 June 2011 |title=Uwe Seemann über die Auflösung des FC Sachsen Leipzig |url=http://www.11freunde.de/interview/uwe-seemann-ueber-die-aufloesung-des-fc-sachsen-leipzig |language=de |newspaper=[[11 Freunde]] |location=Berlin |publisher=11FREUNDE Verlag GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=27 February 2016 |archive-date=7 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190407204144/https://www.11freunde.de/interview/uwe-seemann-ueber-die-aufloesung-des-fc-sachsen-leipzig |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dieckmann |first=Christoph |date=17 October 2013 |title=Heimat aus der Dose |url=http://www.zeit.de/2013/43/fussball-rb-leipzig-red-bull-bundesliga |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref> Red Bull GmbH drew up plans to invest up to 50 million euros in the club. The company planned a takeover, with a change of the team's colours and club name. Involved in the arrangements was film entrepreneur Michael Kölmel, sponsor of FC Sachsen Leipzig and owner of the Zentralstadion.<ref name="AuflösungSachsen"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Matthias |first=Wolf |date=19 December 2006 |title=Sachsen Leipzig soll Flügel bekommen |url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/fussball-sachsen-leipzig-soll-fluegel-bekommen-1383558.html |language=de |newspaper=Frankfurter Allgemeine |location=Frankfurt am Main |publisher=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305174239/https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/fussball-sachsen-leipzig-soll-fluegel-bekommen-1383558.html |archive-date=5 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> By 2006, FC Sachsen Leipzig played in the Oberliga, by then the fourth tier in the [[German football league system]]. Playing in the fourth tier, the club had to undergo the [[German Football Association|German Football Association (DFB)]] licensing procedure. Red Bull GmbH and the club were close to a deal, but the plans were vetoed by the DFB, which rejected the proposed new club name "FC Red Bull Sachsen Leipzig" fearing too much influence from the company.<ref name="AuflösungSachsen"/><ref name="PlantLigaEinstieg">{{cite news |last=Ruf |first=Chrisoph |date=29 May 2009 |title=Rasen Ball Leipzig: Red Bull plant Liga-Einstieg |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/rasen-ball-leipzig-red-bull-plant-liga-einstieg-a-627770.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Pittelkow |first1=Sebastian |last2=Schottner |first2=Dominik |date=17 June 2009 |title=Geld-Revolution auf dem Leipziger Rasen |url=http://www.stern.de/sport/fussball/fussball-sponsoring-von-red-bull-geld-revolution-auf-dem-leipziger-rasen-3813772.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Stern (magazine)|Stern]] |location=Hamburg |publisher=stern.de GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref> After months of fan protests against Red Bull's involvement, which deteriorated into violence, the company officially abandoned the plans.<ref name="Teufel">{{cite news |last=Ruf |first=Christoph |date=17 June 2009 |title=Red Bull in Leipzig: "Wir würden selbst den Teufel mit offenen Armen empfangen" |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/red-bull-in-leipzig-wir-wuerden-selbst-den-teufel-mit-offenen-armen-empfangen-a-630820.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref>

Red Bull GmbH then turned to the former West Germany. The company made contact with [[Hamburg]]-based club [[FC St. Pauli]], and met representatives of the club to discuss a sponsorship deal. A short time before, supporters of FC St. Pauli had participated in protests against Red Bull's takeover of [[SV Austria Salzburg]]. Once it became clear to the Hamburg side that the company had plans that went far beyond conventional sponsoring, it immediately ended the contact, and the question was never considered by the club's management.<ref name="PauliKaufen"/> Red Bull then made contact with [[TSV 1860 Munich]]. Negotiations began behind closed doors, but the club was not interested in an investment and ended the discussions.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=29 April 2014 |title=Red Bull wollte den TSV 1860 übernehmen |url=http://www.abendzeitung-muenchen.de/inhalt.heute-leipzig-damals-muenchen-red-bull-wollte-den-tsv-1860-uebernehmen.dadf2ac8-5dfd-4094-b822-3a6e87e1f285.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Abendzeitung]] |location=Munich |publisher=Abendzeitung München Verlags-GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref><ref name="AndereKandidaten">{{cite web |url=http://www.fussballtransfers.com/2-bundesliga/fortuna-pauli-und-60-red-bull-hatte-andere-kandidaten-und-plane_53555 |title=Fortuna, Pauli und 1860 – Red Bull hatte andere Kandidaten und Pläne |last=Niekamp |first=Kevin |date=29 April 2014 |website=fussballtransfers.com |location=Cologne |publisher=Adversport Germany GmbH |language=de |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref>

In 2007, Red Bull GmbH made plans to invest in [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]], a traditional club with more than 100 years of history.<ref name="FortunaRedBull">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=22 May 2007 |title="Fortuna Red Bull" – die Zukunft? |url=http://www.rp-online.de/sport/fussball/fortuna/fortuna-red-bull-die-zukunft-aid-1.1119525 |newspaper=RP Online |publisher=RP Digital GmbH |location=Düsseldorf |access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref> The plans became public, and it was revealed{{by whom|date=January 2024}} that the company wanted to acquire more than 50 percent of the shares. Rumours spread that the company wanted to rename the club "Red Bull Düsseldorf", or similar. This was immediately met with protests from club supporters.<ref name="PauliKaufen"/> As with FC Sachsen Leipzig, Red Bull's offer also ran into legal difficulties: the statutes of the DFB did not allow changing a club name for advertising purposes, nor for an external investor to obtain a majority share.<ref name="FortunaRedBull"/><ref name="DFBSatzung15§2">{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/fileadmin/_dfbdam/66978-02_Satzung.pdf |title=SATZUNG |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=n.d. |website=dfb.de |publisher=Deutscher Fußball-Bund e.V. |page=12 |language=de |access-date=27 February 2016 |quote=15 § 2: Änderungen, Ergänzungen oder Neugebungen von Vereinsnamen und Vereinszeichen zum Zwecke der Werbung sind unzulässig}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/fileadmin/_dfbdam/66978-02_Satzung.pdf |title=SATZUNG |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=n.d. |website=dfb.de |publisher=Deutscher Fußball-Bund e.V. |page=15 |language=de |access-date=27 February 2016 |quote=16 c § 2: Eine Kapitalgesellschaft kann nur eine Lizenz für die Lizenzligen und damit die Mitgliedschaft im Ligaverband erwerben, wenn ein Verein mehrheitlich an ihr beteiligt ist, der über eine eigene Fußballabteilung verfügt und der im Zeitpunkt, in dem sie sich erstmals für eine Lizenz bewirbt, sportlich für die Teilnahme an einer Lizenzliga qualifiziert ist. Der Verein ("Mutterverein") ist an der Gesellschaft mehrheitlich beteiligt ("Tochtergesellschaft"), wenn er über 50% der Stimmenanteile zuzüglich mindestens eines weiteren Stimmenanteils in der Versammlung der Anteilseigner verfügt. Bei der Kommanditgesellschaft auf Aktien muss der Mutterverein oder eine von ihm zu 100% beherrschte Tochter die Stellung des Komplementärs haben. In diesem Fall genügt ein Stimmenanteil des Muttervereins von weniger als 50%, wenn auf andere Weise sichergestellt ist, dass er eine vergleichbare Stellung hat, wie ein an der Tochtergesellschaft mehrheitlich beteiligter Gesellschafter. Dies setzt insbesondere voraus, dass dem Komplementär die kraft Gesetzes eingeräumte Vertretungsund Geschäftsführungsbefugnis uneingeschränkt zusteht.}}</ref>
Eventually, the plans were soundly rejected by club members.<ref name="PauliKaufen"/><ref name="AndereKandidaten"/> The company began to reconsider the former East Germany.<ref name="PauliKaufen"/>

Leipzig was considered a suitable place for an investment, with the city having a rich history in football, being the meeting place for the founding of the DFB and the home of the first German national football champions, [[VfB Leipzig]].<ref name="Fußballschlaf"/> During East Germany's existence, local teams such as [[1. FC Lokomotive Leipzig]] and its rival, [[BSG Chemie Leipzig (1950)|BSG Chemie Leipzig]], played at the highest level of the [[East German football league system]], and even on the international level. The current state of football there was, however, poor. No team from the city had played in the Bundesliga since 1994,<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=7 January 2016 |title=RB Leipzig: Die Attacke auf den FC Bayern |url=http://www.abendzeitung-muenchen.de/inhalt.bundesliga-und-dann-europa-rb-leipzig-die-attacke-auf-den-fc-bayern.55e790ee-31b5-4aac-9fce-60d9c81f26ed.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Abendzeitung]] |location=Munich |publisher=Abendzeitung München Verlags-GmbH |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref> and no team had played in a professional league since 1998.<ref name="PauliKaufen"/> Its two best teams would soon play in the Oberliga, and local football was plagued by fan violence.<ref name="Fußballschlaf"/> The city hungered for top-level football.<ref name="NewYorkSalzburg">{{cite news |last=Spannagel |first=Lars |date=16 June 2009 |title=New York, Salzburg, Markranstädt: Der RB Leipzig kommt |trans-title=New York, Salzburg, Markranstädt: RB Leipzig is coming |url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/fussball/new-york-salzburg-markranstaedt-der-rb-leipzig-kommt/1536976.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Tagesspiegel |publisher=Verlag Der Tagesspiegel GmbH |location=Berlin}}</ref><ref name="MischtdieBundesliga">{{cite journal |last=Ruf |first=Christoph |date=18 September 2009 |title=Red Bull mischt die Bundesliga auf |url=http://www.merian.de/magazin/leipzig-red-bull-bundesliga.html |language=de |journal=[[Merian (magazine)|Merian]] |publisher=4 Seasons digital.net GmbH |access-date=27 February 2016 |archive-date=11 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311162048/http://www.merian.de/magazin/leipzig-red-bull-bundesliga.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> Leipzig had a population of around 500,000 inhabitants. The city thus had considerable economic strength and fan potential.{{according to whom|date=January 2024}} At the same time, there were no Bundesliga clubs located anywhere near the city, which further strengthened the possibility{{according to whom|date=January 2024}} of attracting sponsors and fans.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}}

Leipzig was fortunate to have a well-developed infrastructure, in the form of [[Leipzig/Halle Airport|an international airport]], motorway connections, and [[Red Bull Arena (Leipzig)|a suitable stadium]].<ref name="WirtschaftsExperte">{{cite web |url=http://www.spox.com/de/sport/fussball/0906/Artikel/tobias-kollmann-red-bull-rasen-ballsport-leipzig-dieter-mateschitz.html |title=Wirtschafts-Experte Tobias Kollmann im Interview: "Ein Erdbeben für den deutschen Fußball" |last=Gruber |first=Haruka |date=16 June 2009 |website=spox.com |publisher=Perform Media Deutschland GmbH |language=de |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref><ref name="DieGruendungVonRB">{{cite news |last=Derßlein |first=Detlef |date=18 November 2009 |title=Die Gründung von RB Leipzig |url=http://www.focus.de/panorama/welt/best-of-playboy/menschen-und-storys/tid-16234/playboy-reportage-die-gruendung-von-rb-leipzig_aid_454906.html |language=de |newspaper=FOCUS Online |location=München |publisher=FOCUS Magazin Verlag GmbH |access-date=28 February 2016 |archive-date=11 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711103325/https://www.focus.de/panorama/welt/best-of-playboy/menschen-und-storys/tid-16234/playboy-reportage-die-gruendung-von-rb-leipzig_aid_454906.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Zentralstadion was a former [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] venue and the second-largest football stadium in the east of Germany, after the [[Olympiastadion (Berlin)|Olympiastadion]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite news |last=Dehne |first=Ulrich |date=17 November 2006 |title=Flügel für die Sachsen? |url=http://www.zeit.de/online/2006/47/red-bull-leipzig |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref>

An investment in a club playing in one of the top divisions in Germany would have been a costly affair for Red Bull. From previous experience, the company knew that the existing traditions of such a club would hinder success in the league.<ref name="RiesigeChance">{{cite news |last=Flohr |first=Sven |date=13 June 2009 |title=Michael Kölmel: "Red Bull ist eine riesige Chance für Leipzig" |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article3918705/Red-Bull-ist-eine-riesige-Chance-fuer-Leipzig.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref> It also knew that an investment in a club playing in one of the top divisions would meet legal difficulties,{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=what sort of legal difficulties? and who from? supporters? club? football authorities?}} making such an investment risky.<ref name="AufEroberungsfeldzug">{{cite news |last=Bunda |first=Sascha |date=16 June 2009 |title=Rasenballsport Leipzig: Red Bull auf Eroberungsfeldzug |url=http://diepresse.com/home/sport/fussball/487564/Rasenballsport-Leipzig_Red-Bull-auf-Eroberungsfeldzug?parentid=564909&showMask=1 |language=de |newspaper=[[Die Presse]] |location=Wien |publisher=Die Presse Verlags-Gesellschaft m.b.H. & Co KG |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Flohr |first1=Sven |last2=Dunker |first2=Robert |date=29 April 2007 |title=Dietrich Mateschitz: Red-Bull-Chef will deutschem Klub Flügel verleihen |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/article839837/Red-Bull-Chef-will-deutschem-Klub-Fluegel-verleihen.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref> Instead, the company found that a newly established club, designed for the company, would be the better option for an investment.<ref name="AndereKandidaten"/><ref name="WirtschaftsExperte"/> Early in 2009, Red Bull GmbH contacted the [[Saxony Football Association|Saxony Football Association (SFV)]], about the procedure to establish a new club in Saxony.<ref name="Teufel"/>

A newly established club would need teams and a playing license. If it did not acquire a license from another club, it would have to start playing in the lowest tier league, the [[Kreisliga|Kreisklasse]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mdr.de/service/impressum/index.html |title=Das Ziel ist ganz klar die Bundesliga |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=4 January 2016 |website=mdr.de |location=Leipzig |publisher=[[Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk]] |language=de |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref> The company searched for a club playing in the [[Oberliga (football)|Oberliga]],<ref name="Teufel"/> since 2008 the fifth tier in the German football league system, and therefore not subject to the DFB licensing system.<ref name="PlantLigaEinstieg"/> On the advice of media entrepreneur Michael Kölmel,<ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/> the company was led to [[SSV Markranstädt]], a small club from a town 13 kilometers west of Leipzig.<ref name="GeldVerleihtFlügel">{{cite news |last1=Pittelkow |first1=Sebastian |last2=Schottner |first2=Dominik |date=15 July 2009 |title=Geld verleiht Flügel |url=https://www.freitag.de/autoren/der-freitag/geld-verleiht-flugel |language=de |newspaper=[[Der Freitag]] |location=Berlin |publisher=der Freitag Mediengesellschaft mbh & Co. KG |access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref> The club was positively inclined to entering a partnership with a global company.<ref name="AufEroberungsfeldzug"/> Its president, Holger Nussbaum, wanted to secure the club's long-term finances, and designed a plan to engage Red Bull GmbH. Holger Nussbaum presented his plan to Kölmel, who saw his chance and decided to join in the deal.<ref name="Fußballschlaf"/><ref name="AufEroberungsfeldzug"/> Assisted by Kölmel, Red Bull GmbH began negotiations with SSV Markranstädt.<ref name="Fußballschlaf"/> Five weeks after the negotiations began, SSV Markranstädt had agreed to sell its licence for the Oberliga to Red Bull GmbH.<ref name="GeldVerleihtFlügel"/> The cost was not disclosed, but SSV Markranstädt is believed to have received a compensation of 350,000 euro.<ref name="DieGruendungVonRB"/><ref name="ImSogdesKapitals">{{cite news |last=Kramer |first=Jörg |date=18 October 2010 |title=Im Sog des Kapitals |url=http://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/d-74549748.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=13 June 2016}}</ref>

''RasenBallsport Leipzig e.V.'' was founded on 19 May 2009. All seven founding members were either employees or agents of Red Bull GmbH.<ref name="Fußballschlaf"/> Andreas Sadlo was elected chairman, and [[Joachim Krug]] was hired as sporting director. Andreas Sadlo, another founding member, was a well-known football player agent, working for the agency "Stars & Friends".<ref name="DerersteNeue">{{cite news |last1=Schmidt |first1=André |last2=Krause |first2=Stefan |date=10 June 2009 |title=Wird er der erste Neue? |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/thomas-klaesener-soll-kommen-8642798.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=20 March 2016}}</ref><ref name="WieeinneuerSponsor">{{cite news |last=Lehmann |first=Marcus |date=16 June 2009 |title=Wie ein neuer Sponsor Flügel verleiht |url=https://www.kicker.de/wie-ein-neuer-sponsor-fluegel-verleiht-510215/artikel |language=de |newspaper=Kicker Online |location=Nuremberg |publisher=Olympia Verlag GmbH |access-date=20 March 2016}}</ref> In order to avoid future objections from the [[German Football Association]] (DFB), Sadlo resigned as player agent, before taking the position of chairman. The statutes of the DFB would not allow a player agent to be involved in the operating affairs of a club.<ref name="Teufel"/> Krug had earlier been employed as coach and manager by [[Rot Weiss Ahlen]], at that time known as ''LR Ahlen'' and sponsored by cosmetics manufacturer LR International.<ref name="OperationBundesliga">{{cite web |url=http://www.sport1.de/de/fussball/artikel_124815.html |title=RB Leipzig startet 'Operation Bundesliga' |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 July 2009 |website=sport1.de |publisher=Sport1 GmbH |location=Ismaning |language=de |access-date=13 June 2016 |archive-date=3 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403015245/http://www.sport1.de/de/fussball/artikel_124815.html |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.spox.com/de/sport/fussball/0907/News/rb-leipzig-startet-operation-bundesliga-fussball.html |title=RB Leipzig startet "Operation Bundesliga-Fußball" |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 July 2009 |website=spox.com |publisher=Perform Media Deutschland GmbH |language=de |access-date=11 June 2016}}</ref><ref name="DorfvereinFlügel">{{cite news |last=Ruf |first=Christoph |date=25 September 2009 |title=RB Leipzig: Wenn ein Dorfverein Flügel bekommt |url=http://www.zeit.de/sport/fussball/2009-09/lok-leipzig-red-bull |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=13 June 2016}}</ref>

RB Leipzig became the fifth football commitment in the Red Bull sporting portfolio, following [[FC Red Bull Salzburg]] in Austria, the [[New York Red Bulls]] in the United States, [[Red Bull Brasil|Red Bull Brasil (now Red Bull Bragantino II)]] in Brazil and [[Red Bull Ghana]] in Ghana.<ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/> In contrast with previous clubs, RB Leipzig did not bear the corporate name. The statutes of the DFB would not permit a corporate name to be included in the club name.<ref name="DFBSatzung15§2"/><ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/> Instead, the club adopted the unusual name ''RasenBallsport'', literally meaning "Lawn Ball Sports". By using the initials "RB", as in "Red Bull",<ref name="Fußballschlaf"/> the corporate identity could still be recognized.<ref name="DorfvereinFlügel"/><ref name="Independent1">{{cite news |last=Paterson |first=Tony |date=24 June 2009 |title=East German football gets the kick it needs |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/east-german-football-gets-the-kick-it-needs-1716000.html |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Vetter |first=Claus |date=13 September 2013 |title=RB Leipzig Die guten Bullen |url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/rb-leipzig-die-guten-bullen/8782038.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Tagesspiegel |publisher=Verlag Der Tagesspiegel GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=7 August 2015}}</ref>

RB Leipzig began as a partnership with fifth-division side SSV Markranstädt. The partnership meant that SSV Markranstädt would provide the initial core of RB Leipzig, as the starting point for RB's leap into German football.<ref name="PlantLigaEinstieg"/><ref name="Teufel"/> RB Leipzig acquired a playing license for the Oberliga, the top three men's teams and a senior men's team from SSV Markranstädt.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=what does it mean 'the top three men's teams'?}}<ref name="PlantLigaEinstieg"/><ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/><ref name="DerersteNeue"/><ref name="WieeinneuerSponsor"/> The first team was completely taken over, with its training staff and its head coach, Tino Vogel, son of former East German footballer [[Eberhard Vogel]].<!--was Vogel fired or hired?-->{{clarify|date=April 2023}}<ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/><ref name="Zeit1"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Stahmer |first=K. |date=23 June 2009 |title=Der Markranstädt-Trainer: Fliegt RB auf Vogel? |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/trainer-tino-vogel-im-interview-8775480.bild.html |newspaper=Bild |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |location=Berlin |access-date=6 August 2015}}</ref>

The transfer of the licence for the Oberliga had to be approved by the [[North East German Football Association]] (NOFV). RB Leipzig would need at least four junior teams, including an A-junior team, to obtain the licence. In the deal, SSV Markranstädt had kept its junior department, and RB Leipzig lacked junior teams. Red Bull GmbH therefore approached FC Sachsen Leipzig. The club was experiencing financial issues, and could no longer finance its youth department.<ref name="DerersteNeue"/> The NOFV approved the transfer of the playing right on 13 June 2009, and RB Leipzig was given one year to complete its stable of junior teams.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://leipzig-seiten.de/index.php/kultur-unterhaltung-2/32-sport/fussball/11570-nofv-erteilt-spielgenehmigung-fberliga-teilnahme-von-rb-Leipzig |title=NOFV erteilt Spielgenehmigung für Oberliga-Teilnahme von RB Leipzig |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=13 June 2009 |website=leipzig-seiten.de |location=Leipzig |publisher=LE-news-NET UG |language=de |access-date=20 March 2016 |archive-date=12 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210712045034/https://leipzig-seiten.de/index.php/kultur-unterhaltung-2/32-sport/fussball/11570-nofv-erteilt-spielgenehmigung-fberliga-teilnahme-von-rb-Leipzig |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=14 June 2009 |title=Red Bull soll Leipziger Fußball Flügel verleihen |url=http://www.badische-zeitung.de/f-allgemein/red-bull-soll-leipziger-fussball-fluegel-verleihen--16034078.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Badische Zeitung]] |location=Freiburg im Breisgau |publisher=Badischer Verlag GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=20 March 2016}}</ref> The club then acquired four junior teams from FC Sachsen Leipzig.<ref name="nehmenAnlauf">{{cite news |last=Volker |first=Makus |date=3 August 2009 |title=Bullen nehmen Anlauf |url=http://www.taz.de/!5158708/ |language=de |newspaper=Die Tageszeitung |location=Berlin |publisher=taz Verlags u. Vertriebs GmbH |access-date=20 March 2016}}</ref> The [[Saxony Football Association|Saxony Football Association (SFV)]] urged the acquisition, in order to prevent a talent exodus.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=1 August 2009 |title=Reichenbach sieht keine Bevorzugung von RB Leipzig |url=http://www.rp-online.de/sport/fussball/reichenbach-sieht-keine-bevorzugung-von-rb-leipzig-aid-1.2447267 |newspaper=RP Online |publisher=RP Digital GmbH |location=Düsseldorf |access-date=6 August 2015}}</ref>
[[File:Ralph Hasenhüttl (2016).jpg|thumb|[[Ralph Hasenhüttl]], the club's first manager in the Bundesliga]]

RB Leipzig would play its inaugural season in the Oberliga at the Stadion am Bad in Markranstädt. The stadium held 5,000 seats and traditionally the home ground of SSV Markranstädt. The plans were for the club to soon move to the far larger Zentralstadion,<ref name="PlantLigaEinstieg"/> hopefully in 2010, after advancing to the Regionalliga.<ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/><ref name="RiesigeChance"/> The stadium was owned by Michael Kölmel, who had been known to Red Bull GmbH for years and had, as a negotiation partner, facilitated the establishment of RB Leipzig.<ref name="Fußballschlaf"/><ref name="RiesigeChance"/> Michael Kölmel had himself been involved in local football previously, as a sponsor of FC Sachsen Leipzig. He was eager to find a strong tenant for the stadium, which last saw FC Sachsen Leipzig play in the Regionalliga behind closed doors.{{clarify|date=April 2023}}<ref name="RiesigeChance"/><ref name="Zeit1">{{cite news |last=Spannagel |first=Lars |date=16 June 2009 |title=Investor Red Bull: In acht Jahren in die Bundesliga |url=http://www.zeit.de/online/2009/25/red-bull-leipzig-mateschitz-dfb |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=20 March 2016}}</ref> Negotiations between Red Bull GmbH and Michael Kölmel began immediately upon the club's founding. Red Bull GmbH reserved the naming right to the stadium in June 2009, meaning that the name could not be sold to another company.<ref name="MischtdieBundesliga"/><ref name="RiesigeChance"/><ref name="AufEroberungsfeldzug"/><ref name="BlühendenFußballLandschaft">{{cite news |last=Horeni |first=Michael |date=26 June 2009 |title=Versprechen einer blühenden Fußball-Landschaft |url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/rasen-ball-leipzig-versprechen-einer-bluehenden-fussball-landschaft-1811273.html |language=de |newspaper=Frankfurter Allgemeine |location=Frankfurt am Main |publisher=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung GmbH |access-date=20 March 2016}}</ref>

On its founding, RB Leipzig aimed to play first-division Bundesliga football within eight years, following the model previously used by Red Bull GmbH in Austria and the United States.<ref name="Zeit1"/><ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/> It was predicted{{by whom|date=January 2024}} that Red Bull GmbH would invest 100 million euro in the club over a period of ten years, and Mateschitz openly spoke of the possibility of ultimately winning the German championship.<ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/><ref name="Independent1"/><ref name="Zeit1"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://archiv.sport1.de/de/fussball/artikel_121784.html |title=Mateschitz: Titel mit RB Leipzig prinzipiell möglich |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=24 June 2009 |website=sport1.de |publisher=Sport1 GmbH |location=Ismaning |language=de |access-date=5 August 2015}}{{Dead link|date=July 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> The last team from Leipzig to do so was [[VfB Leipzig]] in 1913.<ref name="Fußballschlaf"/>

===2009–2016: Rise through the divisions===
After some previously scheduled games had to be canceled due to safety concerns, RB Leipzig played its first match on 10 July 2009, a friendly match against the [[Landesliga]] club SV Bannewitz.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The match was played at the Stadion am Bad in [[Markranstädt]] and ended with a 5–0 win for RB Leipzig. The club played its first competitive match on 31 July 2009, in the first round of the [[Saxony Cup]] against VfK Blau–Weiß Leipzig, winning 5–0.<ref name="bundesligahistoryofrb">{{cite web |title=From the fifth division to the UEFA Champions League semi-finals in 11 years: the history of RB Leipzig |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/history-of-rb-leipzig-from-fifth-division-to-champions-league-nagelsmann-rangnick-12466 |publisher=Bundesliga |access-date=16 November 2024 |language=en |date=7 August 2022}}</ref> The club then played its first league match away to [[FC Carl Zeiss Jena|FC Carl Zeiss Jena II]] on 8 August 2009. The match ended 1–1.<ref name="bundesligahistoryofrb" />

During the further course of the season, RB Leipzig suffered its first defeat on 13 September 2009, in a match against [[Budissa Bautzen]].{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The club was claimed the title of ''[[Herbstmeister]]'', as they stood in first place after the first half of the 2009–10 season.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The team returned for the second half of the season stronger, having signed the experienced midfielder and 2. Bundesliga player [[Timo Rost]] from [[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]] in January 2010.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=5 January 2010 |title=RB Leipzig verstärkt sich mit Timo Rost |url=http://www.focus.de/sport/fussball/wm–2010/national–rb–leipzig–verstaerkt–sich–mit–timo–rost_aid_468173.html |language=de |newspaper=FOCUS Online |location=München |publisher=FOCUS Magazin Verlag GmbH |access-date=24 October 2015 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The team secured first place in the 2009–10 NOFV–Oberliga Süd at the 25th matchday, thus earning promotion to the 2010–11 [[Regionalliga Nord]]. The team finished the season with a goal difference of +57 (74 scored and 17 conceded), having suffered only two defeats.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oberliga bis 12/13 – Deutschland – Herren – 2009/2010: Ergebnisse, Tabelle und Spielplan |url=https://www.fussball.de/spieltagsuebersicht/nofv-oberliga-sued-deutschland-oberliga-bis-12-13-herren-saison0910-deutschland/-/staffel/012SBT885O000000VV0AG813VTSS985H-G#!/ |website=www.fussball.de |access-date=16 November 2024 |language=de |date=29 May 2010}}</ref> The playing right for the Regionalliga was issued by the DFB on 4 May 2010.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} RB Leipzig targeted a place in the 2010–11 DFB–Pokal, which would have been won by winning the 2009–10 Saxony Cup.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The team reached the quarterfinals in the Saxony Cup, but was eliminated after a defeat against [[FSV Zwickau]] on 13 November 2009.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}}

The incumbent chairman, Andreas Saldo, left the club in January 2010<ref>{{cite web |url=http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_110.html |title=Andreas Sadlo verlässt RB Leipzig |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=15 January 2010 |website=redbulls.com |publisher=Red Bull GmbH |location=Fuschl am See |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100118092850/http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_110.html |archive-date=18 January 2010 |access-date=24 October 2015}}</ref> and the position was assumed by the former [[Hamburger SV]] sporting director and incumbent sporting director for the common Red Bull football commitment [[Dietmar Beiersdorfer]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_137.html |title=RB Leipzig zieht in neue Geschäftsstelle |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=24 February 2010 |website=redbulls.com |publisher=Red Bull GmbH |location=Fuschl am See |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100228160418/http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_137.html |archive-date=28 February 2010 |access-date=24 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=24 February 2010 |title=Beiersdorfer neuer Boss bei RB Leipzig |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article6541993/Beiersdorfer–neuer–Boss–bei–RB–Leipzig.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=24 October 2015}}</ref> One day after the last match of the 2009–10 season, Beiersdorfer released head coach Tino Vogel, assistant coach Lars Weißenberger and sporting director Joachim Krug from their positions.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=30 May 2010 |title=Tino Vogel muss als Cheftrainer bei RB Leipzig gehen – Sportdirektor Krug freigestellt |url=http://oberliga.lvz-online.de/lvzs.site,postext,aktuell-rb,artikel_id,22376.html |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags– und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100602032222/http://oberliga.lvz-online.de/lvzs.site,postext,aktuell-rb,artikel_id,22376.html |archive-date =2 June 2010 |access-date=24 October 2015}}</ref> This action was done after Red Bull owner Dietrich Mateschitz had announced a change in strategy. According to the new strategy, RB Leipzig was going to represent the key project in the football commitment of the company, in place of FC Red Bull Salzburg.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=10 May 2010 |title=Mateschitz will das große Geld lieber in Leipzig investieren |url=http://www.krone.at/Sport/Mateschitz_will_das_grosse_Geld_lieber_in_Leipzig_investieren–Nur_U21_in_Salzburg–Story–199223 |language=de |newspaper=Kronen Zeitung |location=Wien |publisher=Krone Multimedia GmbH & Co KG |access-date=24 October 2015}}</ref> Tomas Oral was announced as the new head coach on 18 June 2010.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}}

The players Christian Mittenzwei, [[Sebastian Hauck]], Stefan Schumann, Toni Jurascheck and [[Michael Lerchl]] did not receive new contracts for the following Regionalliga season, while players Frank Räbsch, Ronny Kujat and two other players ended their careers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_171.html |title=RBL–Gala zum Abschied von Markranstädt |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=22 May 2010 |website=redbulls.com |publisher=Red Bull GmbH |location=Fuschl am See |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100529051943/http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_171.html |archive-date =29 May 2010 |access-date=24 October 2015}}</ref>
