Before entry to the Regionalliga, there were two significant changes in the club. The club returned the second, third and fourth team to SSV Markranstädt. In order to replace the reserve team, the club adopted the first team of ESV Delitzsch as its reserve team and purchased its playing right for the [[Bezirksliga|Bezirksliga Leipzig]].<ref name="StelltWeichen">{{cite web |url=http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_176.html |title=Regionalligist RB Leipzig stellt Weichen |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=30 May 2010 |website=redbulls.com |publisher=Red Bull GmbH |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100603145429/http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_176.html |archive-date=3 June 2010 |access-date=7 August 2015}}</ref> The first team moved from the Stadion am Bad in [[Markranstädt]], to make the Zentralstadion in Leipzig its new home arena. The former 2006 FIFA World Cup venue was simultaneously renamed Red Bull Arena.<ref name="Teufel"/><ref name="Guardian1">{{cite news |last=Oltermann |first=Philip |date=17 June 2009 |title=Why RB Leipzig are sending shockwaves through German football |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/mar/06/rb-leipzig-sending-shockwaves-through-german-football |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |access-date=12 June 2016}}</ref> The opening of the Red Bull Arena was celebrated on 24 July 2010 with a friendly match against the German vice-champions [[FC Schalke 04]] in front of 21,566 spectators. The match ended with a 1–2 loss for RB Leipzig.<ref name="ArenaEröffnung">{{cite web |url=http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_213.html |title=RBL feiert gelungene Arena-Eröffnung |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=24 July 2010 |website=redbulls.com |publisher=Red Bull GmbH |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100826040927/http://redbulls.com/soccer/leipzig/de/rb-leipzig-news-detail_213.html |archive-date=26 August 2010 |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref> The first team played its last game at the Stadion am Bad six days later on 30 July 2010, a friendly match against [[Hertha BSC]], which ended with a 2–1 win for RB Leipzig.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}}

The 2010–11 Regionalliga season started with a series of draws, the first one on 6 August 2010 against [[Türkiyemspor Berlin]] in front of 4,028 spectators at the Red Bull Arena. The first win came at the 4th matchday, in an away match against [[Holstein Kiel]], which ended 1–2 for RB Leipzig. The first home win came immediately after, at the 5th matchday, in a match against [[1. FC Magdeburg]], which ended 2–1 for RB Leipzig. After a quiet start to the season, the club found itself chasing [[Chemnitzer FC]], themselves also seeking promotion. At the end of the year, RB Leipzig confirmed its ambitions to gain promotion, by signing Brazilian midfielder [[Thiago Rockenbach]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Roth |first=Andreas |date=6 January 2011 |title=RB will mit Rockenbach da Silva angreifen – Oral bittet zwei Wochen in die Türkei |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/RB-will-mit-Rockenbach-da-Silva-angreifen-Oral-bittet-zwei-Wochen-in-die-Tuerkei |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=25 October 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012853/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/RB-will-mit-Rockenbach-da-Silva-angreifen-Oral-bittet-zwei-Wochen-in-die-Tuerkei |url-status=dead}}</ref> The club had signed forward [[Carsten Kammlott]], considered{{by whom|date=January 2024}} a promising young talent, and the experienced Leipzig-born defender [[Tim Sebastian (footballer)|Tim Sebastian]], during the summer.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Krause |first1=S. |last2=Windisch |first2=M. |date=6 July 2010 |title=Super-Talent Kammlott stürmt zu den Bullen |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/leipzig/super-talent-carsten-kammlott-stuermt-zu-den-bullen-13197078.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=16 June 2010 |title=RB Leipzig – Sebastian kommt aus Rostock |url=http://www.reviersport.de/121285---rb-leipzig-tim-sebastian-kommt-aus-rostock.html |language=de |newspaper=Revier Sport |location=Essen |publisher=RevierSport online GmbH |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref>

The club finished its first season in the Regionalliga in 4th place, thus missing out on promotion. However, under coach Tomas Oral, the club succeeded in winning the 2010–11 Saxony Cup after defeating [[Chemnitzer FC]] 1–0 in the final on 1 June 2011 in front of 13,958 spectators at the Red Bull Arena. By winning the 2010–11 Saxony Cup, the club won its first title in club history. It also qualified to participate in the [[2011–12 DFB-Pokal]].<ref name="SächsischeZeitung">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=1 June 2011 |title=RB Leipzig gewinnt Sachsen-Pokal |url=http://www.sz-online.de/sachsen/regionalsport/rb-leipzig-gewinnt-sachsen-pokal-757166.html |language=de |newspaper=Sächsische Zeitung |location=Dresden |publisher=Sächsische Zeitung GmbH |access-date=25 October 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304053647/http://www.sz-online.de/sachsen/regionalsport/rb-leipzig-gewinnt-sachsen-pokal-757166.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> Because the club missed out on promotion during the second half of the 2010–11 season, [[Peter Pacult]] from [[Rapid Wien]] was announced as the new head coach for the 2011–12 season on 4 May 2011. Almost simultaneously, the club announced that sporting director [[Thomas Linke]] had been released from his position, having been employed for only 10 weeks, from February 2011. Various media suspected a connection between the signing of Pacult and the departure of Linke.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=4 May 2011 |title=Nur kurze Amtszeit – Linke verlässt RB Leipzig |url=http://www.n-tv.de/sport/fussball/Linke-verlaesst-RB-Leipzig-article3256146.html |language=de |newspaper=n-tv |location=Cologne |publisher=n-tv Nachrichtenfernsehen GmbH |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.spox.com/de/sport/fussball/regionalliga/1105/News/peter-pacult-neuer-trainer-bei-viertligist-rb-leipzig-ruecktritt-von-sportdirektor-thomas-linke.html |title=Rücktritt von Sportdirektor Thomas Linke – Pacult: Leipzig ist "höchstinteressante" Aufgabe |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=5 May 2015 |website=spox.com |location=Unterföhring |publisher=Perform Media Deutschland GmbH |language=de |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref>

Also, several players left the team, among them [[Lars Müller]], [[Sven Neuhaus]], [[Thomas Kläsener]] and [[Nico Frommer]], all participants in the previous Saxony Cup final.<ref name="SächsischeZeitung"/> With Daniel Rosin, Timo Rost and Benjamin Bellot, only three players from the former Oberliga team remained in the team for the 2011–12 Regionalliga season, while the former international [[Ingo Hertzsch]] as a fourth of these players remained in the club.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='only three'? 'while...a fourth of these players'? the fourth of three? what?}} Hertzsch ended his professional career after the 2010–11 season, but went on to join the reserve team, RB Leipzig II, and the RB Leipzig business operation.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=31 May 2011 |title=Hertzsch beendet Karriere, bleibt aber bei RB |url=https://www.kicker.de/hertzsch-beendet-karriere-bleibt-aber-bei-rb-553302/artikel |language=de |newspaper=Kicker Online |location=Nuremberg |publisher=Olympia-Verlag GmbH |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref> On 29 July 2011, RB Leipzig made its debut in the [[DFB-Pokal]], in front of 31,212 spectators at the Red Bull Arena. The team knocked Bundesliga club [[VfL Wolfsburg]] out of the first round of the cup, beating them 3–2 after a [[hat-trick]] by [[Daniel Frahn]].<ref name="LeipzigschmeißtWolfsburg">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=29 July 2011 |title=DFB-Pokal: Viertligist Leipzig schmeißt Wolfsburg raus |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/dfb-pokal-viertligist-leipzig-schmeisst-wolfsburg-raus-a-777450.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref> The team was eliminated in the next round, defeated 0–1 by [[FC Augsburg]]. The 2011–12 Regionalliga season saw the largest win in club history, when RB Leipzig defeated [[SV Wilhelmshaven]] 8–2 on 19 February 2012.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=19 February 2012 |title=Torfestival in der Red-Bull-Arena: RB Leipzig schlägt den SV Wilhelmshaven mit 8:2 |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Torfestival-in-der-Red-Bull-Arena-RB-Leipzig-schlaegt-den-SV-Wilhelmshaven-mit-8-2 |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckerei-Verwaltungs-GmbH |access-date=25 October 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012930/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Torfestival-in-der-Red-Bull-Arena-RB-Leipzig-schlaegt-den-SV-Wilhelmshaven-mit-8-2 |url-status=dead}}</ref> After a decisive 2–2 draw against [[VfL Wolfsburg|VfL Wolfsburg II]] at the 33rd matchday, the club missed out on promotion for the second time in the Regionalliga, finishing the season in 3rd place.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}}
[[File:Ralf Rangnick 2011 2.jpg|thumb|right|Ralf Rangnick in 2011, as head coach of Schalke 04]]

The 2012–13 season in the reformed [[Regionalliga Nordost]] began with major personnel changes. Former [[Schalke 04]] head coach [[Ralf Rangnick]] was introduced as the new sporting director. Coinciding with his arrival, he replaced head coach Peter Pacult with former [[SG Sonnenhof Großaspach]] coach [[Alexander Zorniger]].<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 July 2012 |title=RB Leipzig: Trainerwechsel beim Viertligisten – Rangnick entlässt Pacult, Zorniger schon da |url=https://www.kicker.de/rangnick-entlaesst-pacult-zorniger-schon-da-571346/artikel |language=de |newspaper=Kicker Online |location=Nuremberg |publisher=Olympia-Verlag GmbH |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=6 July 2012 |title=Rangnick: "Neue Zeitrechnung" |url=https://www.kicker.de/rangnick_neue-zeitrechnung-571386/artikel |language=de |newspaper=Kicker Online |location=Nuremberg |publisher=Olympia-Verlag GmbH |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref> The season proved more successful than the previous two. The club won the ''Herbstmeister'' title with two matchdays left of the first half of the season, after defeating [[FSV Zwickau]] 1–0 away.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The team then secured first place in the 2012–13 Regionalliga Nordost at the 18th matchday, after the second placed club [[FC Carl Zeiss Jena]] lost a match against [[Berliner AK 07]] on 7 May 2013 and, as a consequence, were no longer able to overtake RB.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}}

The 2012–13 Saxony Cup was another success. The club reached the final for the second time in club history and, as in 2011, the opponent was Chemnitzer FC. The team won the final on 15 May 2013 by 4–2 in front of 16,864 spectators at the Red Bull Arena. The crowd number set a new record for a Saxony Cup final, breaking the previous record from 2011. By winning the 2012–13 Saxony Cup, the club was also qualified to participate in the 2013–14 DFB-Pokal.<ref name="PackendesFinale">{{cite news |last=Grimm |first=Anne |date=15 May 2013 |title=Packendes Finale im Sachsenpokal – RB Leipzig bezwingt Chemnitz und holt den Pott |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Packendes-Finale-im-Sachsenpokal-RB-Leipzig-bezwingt-Chemnitz-und-holt-den-Pott |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=25 October 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012918/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Packendes-Finale-im-Sachsenpokal-RB-Leipzig-bezwingt-Chemnitz-und-holt-den-Pott |url-status=dead}}</ref> As the winner of the 2012–13 Regionallig Nordost, RB Leipzig won a place in the qualification for the [[3. Liga]]. The club was drawn against [[Sportfreunde Lotte]] from the [[Regionalliga West]]. RB Leipzig won the first leg on 29 May 2013 by 2–0. The match was played at the Red Bull Arena in front of 30,104 spectators, a crowd number which set a new record for matches in the 4th division.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=29 May 2013 |title=Für Regionalliga Weltklasse |url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/fussball-fuer-regionalliga-weltklasse-12200952.html |language=de |newspaper=Frankfurter Allgemeine |location=Frankfurt am Main |publisher=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung GmbH |access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref><ref name="RekordKulisse">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=29 May 2014 |title=Relegations-Hinspiel zur dritten Liga: Leipzig siegt vor Rekord-Kulisse |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig-siegt-vor-rekord-kulisse-gegen-lotte-a-902684.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref>

The second leg was played on 2 June 2013 and ended 2–2 after two goals to RB Leipzig during extra time.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The result meant that RB Leipzig had finally won promotion to the 3. Liga, after three seasons in the Regionalliga. In the [[2013–14 RB Leipzig season|2013–14 season]], RB Leipzig made its first appearance in the 3. Liga in club history.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The club signed [[Anthony Jung]] from [[FSV Frankfurt]], [[Tobias Willers]] from Sportfreunde Lotte, [[Joshua Kimmich]] from the U19 team of [[VfB Stuttgart]], [[André Luge]] from FSV Zwickau, [[Christos Papadimitriou (footballer)|Christos Papadimitriou]] from [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]], [[Yussuf Poulsen]] from [[Lyngby BK]] and [[Denis Thomalla]] from [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim]] during the summer.

RB Leipzig was eliminated by [[FC Augsburg]] in the first round of the [[2013–14 DFB-Pokal]] on 2 August 2013 after losing 0–2 at the Red Bull Arena.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The defeat brought an end to a year-long series without defeat in competitive matches.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The 2013–14 3. Liga had a more promising start. The team won its first match, against [[Hallescher FC]] away, by 1–0 on 19 July 2013 and kept an undefeated streak until 31 August 2013, when the team lost 1–2 to first placed team [[SV Wehen Wiesbaden]] away.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} On 5 October 2013, RB Leipzig again met the first placed team.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} SV Wehen Wiesbaden had lost its first-place position to [[1. FC Heidenheim]] only one week after its defeat of RB Leipzig.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} 1. FC Heidenheim would defend it until the end of the season.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} RB Leipzig defeated 1. FC Heidenheim by 2–0 after a convincing{{according to whom|date=January 2024}} performance at the [[Voith-Arena]] and climbed to third place.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} During the winter break, players Christos Papadimitriou, [[Juri Judt]], Carsten Kammlott and [[Bastian Schulz]] left the team.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} In return, the team was joined by [[Diego Demme]] from [[SC Paderborn 07]], [[Federico Palacios Martínez]] from [[VfL Wolfsburg]], [[Mikko Sumusalo]] from [[HJK Helsinki]] and [[Georg Teigl]] from [[FC Red Bull Salzburg]].
[[File:Georg teigl15.JPG|right|thumb|Georg Teigl playing a match for FC Red Bull Salzburg in May 2013]]

After losing 1–2 away to [[MSV Duisburg]] on 1 February 2014, the team would not concede a single defeat for the rest of the season.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} A thrilling duel with [[SV Darmstadt 98]] appeared,{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='appeared'?}} with both teams fighting for the crucial second place. The two teams met at the 35th matchday, on 19 April 2014. RB Leipzig came out as the winner, defeating SV Darmstadt 98 by 1–0 in front of 39,147 spectators at the Red Bull Arena.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=19 April 2014 |title=RB dank Jungs Hammer näher am Ziel |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-darmstadt-2014-liga-1897434/analyse |language=de |newspaper=Kicker Online |location=Nuremberg |publisher=Olympia-Verlag GmbH |access-date=31 October 2015}}</ref> RB Leipzig secured the second place and direct promotion to the [[2. Bundesliga]] two weeks later, after defeating last placed team [[1. FC Saarbrücken]] 5–1 in front of a nearly sold out Red Bull Arena on 3 May 2014. The crowd of 42,713 spectators set a new club record.<ref name="Durchmarschin2.Fußball">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 May 2014 |title=Aufgestiegen – RB Leipzig schafft Durchmarsch in 2. Fußball-Bundesliga |url=http://www.morgenpost.de/sport/article127584655/RB-Leipzig-schafft-Durchmarsch-in-2-Fussball-Bundesliga.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Berliner Morgenpost]] |location=Berlin |publisher=Berliner Morgenpost GmbH |access-date=31 October 2015}}</ref><ref name="Saarbrücken">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 May 2015 |title=RB Leipzig macht Aufstieg in die 2. Liga perfekt |url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/5-1-gegen-saarbruecken-rb-leipzig-macht-aufstieg-in-die-2-liga-perfekt/9839912.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Der Tagesspiegel]] |location=Berlin |publisher=Verlag Der Tagesspiegel GmbH |access-date=31 October 2015}}</ref>

By finishing the season in second place, RB Leipzig won promotion to the 2. Bundesliga and became the first team since the introduction of the 3. Liga to win promotion to the 2. Bundesliga after only one season.<ref name="Saarbrücken"/><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 May 2014 |title=RB Leipzig schreibt mit Aufstieg Geschichte |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article127579165/RB-Leipzig-schreibt-mit-Aufstieg-Geschichte.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Die Welt]] |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=31 October 2015}}</ref> Following promotion to the 2. Bundesliga, the organization responsible for licensing was no longer the DFB, but instead the [[Deutsche Fußball Liga|German Football League (DFL)]]. The DFL announced its first decision in the licensing process on 22 April 2014. RB Leipzig was to be given a license for the [[2014–15 2. Bundesliga|2014–15 2. Bundesliga season]], but only under certain conditions.<ref name="Kicker">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=25 April 2014 |title=RB Leipzig muss bei Aufstieg sein Logo ändern |url=https://www.kicker.de/rb-leipzig-muss-bei-aufstieg-sein-logo-aendern-603363/artikel |language=de |newspaper=Kicker Online |location=Nuremberg |publisher=Olympia-Verlag GmbH |access-date=29 December 2015}}</ref> Criticism mounted that the club lacked in participation, that club management was too concentrated in only a handful of people<ref name="taz.de">{{cite news |last=Henning |first=John |date=3 May 2014 |title=Fußballklub RB Leipzig – DFL verleiht Flügel |url=http://www.taz.de/!5043233/ |language=de |newspaper=Die Tageszeitung |location=Berlin |publisher=taz Verlags u. Vertriebs GmbH |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> and that the club was not independent enough from Red Bull GmbH.<ref name="Kicker"/> To ensure independence and improve participation, the DFL set up three requirements that the club had to meet in order to obtain a license for the 2014–15 2. Bundesliga season.<ref name="taz.de"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Wöckener |first=Lutz |date=29 May 2014 |title=Die überraschende Nachsicht der DFL mit RB Leipzig |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article128505732/Die-ueberraschende-Nachsicht-der-DFL-mit-RB-Leipzig.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> One of the requirements was to redesign the crest, as the crest too closely resembled the corporate logo of Red Bull GmbH. A second requirement was to change the composition of the club's organizational bodies.<ref name="l-iz.de"/> A third requirement was to lower the membership fees and open up the association for new members.<ref name="leipzig.sportbuzzer.de">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=24 April 2014 |title=Medienbericht: RB Leipzig muss Logo und Vorstandsriege ändern – Mitgliedsbeitrag zu hoch |url=http://www.sportbuzzer.de/artikel/medienbericht-rb-leipzig-muss-logo-und-vorstandsriege-andern-mitgliedsbeitrag-zu/ |language=de |newspaper=Sportbuzzer |location=Hannover |publisher=Sportbuzzer GmbH |access-date=29 April 2017 |archive-date=21 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521032053/https://www.sportbuzzer.de/artikel/medienbericht-rb-leipzig-muss-logo-und-vorstandsriege-andern-mitgliedsbeitrag-zu/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> The German legal magazine ''[[Legal Tribune Online]]'' assessed all three requirements set up by the DFL as legally questionable.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lto.de/recht/hintergruende/h/rb-leipzig-aufstieg-lizenz/?googlenews=1&cHash=7605bfd87f5ea70bd1512bcd8dd18c35 |title=Red Bull belbt ostdeutschen Fußall wieder |last=Arnhold |first=Johannes |date=29 April 2014 |website=lto.de |location=Cologne |publisher=Wolters Kluwer Deutschland GmbH |language=de |access-date=29 December 2015 |archive-date=3 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161203094137/http://www.lto.de/recht/hintergruende/h/rb-leipzig-aufstieg-lizenz/?googlenews=1&cHash=7605bfd87f5ea70bd1512bcd8dd18c35 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

RB Leipzig filed an appeal on 30 April 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.liga3-online.de/leipzig-legt-beschwerde-gegen-lizenz-auflagen-ein/ |title=RB Leipzig legt Beschwerde gegen Lizenz-Auflagen ein |last=Koch |first=Julian |date=30 April 2014 |website=liga3-online.de |location=Hamburg |publisher=mediasports Digital GmbH |language=de |access-date=29 December 2015}}</ref> Sporting director Ralf Rangnick appeared in the media and suggested compromise with the DFL, stating that what the jerseys look like were not as important as those who would be wearing them.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 May 2014 |title=RB Leipzig im Lizenzverfahren zu Kompromissen bereit |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/fussball-3-liga-rb-leipzig-im-lizenzverfahren-zu-kompromissen-bereit/9835988.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Handelsblatt]] |location=Düsseldorf |publisher=Handelsblatt GmbH |access-date=29 December 2015 |quote=Wenn die DFL will, dass wir das Logo ändern, dann werden wir das tun. Es ist nicht wichtig, was auf dem Trikot steht, sondern was drin ist |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305134655/http://www.handelsblatt.com/fussball-3-liga-rb-leipzig-im-lizenzverfahren-zu-kompromissen-bereit/9835988.html |archive-date=5 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The appeal was rejected in a second decision by the DFL on 8 May 2014.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=8 May 2014 |title=Zweitliga-Aufsteiger: DFL lehnt Beschwerde von RB Leipzig ab |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/2-fussball-bundesliga-dfl-lehnt-beschwerde-von-rb-leipzig-ab-a-968240.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |location=Hamburg |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |access-date=29 December 2015}}</ref> Red Bull GmbH owner Dietrich Mateschitz spoke out in media, openly criticizing the decision by the DFL. He described the requirements as a "[[decapitation]] request" and categorically rejected another season in the 3. Liga, ultimately threatening to end the project in Leipzig if the license was not given.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=8 May 2014 |title=LVZ-Exklusiv: RB-Lizenz wackelt – Mateschitz schäumt |url=http://www.sportbuzzer.de/artikel/lvz-exklusiv-rb-lizenz-wackelt-mateschitz-schaumt/ |language=de |newspaper=Sportbuzzer |location=Hannover |publisher=Sportbuzzer GmbH |access-date=29 April 2017 |archive-date=12 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210712055821/https://www.sportbuzzer.de/artikel/lvz-exklusiv-rb-lizenz-wackelt-mateschitz-schaumt/ |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=8 May 2014 |title=Mateschitz nach Attacke gegen RB Leipzig geschockt |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article127772305/Mateschitz-nach-Attacke-gegen-RB-Leipzig-geschockt.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=30 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport1.de/de/fussball/fussball_bundesliga2/newspage_887994.html |title=Lizenz: RB Leipzig droht das Aus |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=8 May 2015 |website=sport1.de |publisher=Sport1 GmbH |location=Ismaning |language=de |access-date=30 December 2015 |archive-date=3 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170203104449/http://www.sport1.de/de/fussball/fussball_bundesliga2/newspage_887994.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>

RB Leipzig filed a second appeal on 12 May 2014.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=12 May 2014 |title=Aufsteiger RB Leipzig legt erneut Beschwerde ein |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article127899758/Aufsteiger-RB-Leipzig-legt-erneut-Beschwerde-ein.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=30 December 2015}}</ref> The DFL licensing committee was set to make a decision on the second appeal on 15 May 2014, before making its final decision on 28 May 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.t-online.de/sport/fussball/id_69380828/rb-leipzig-legt-erneut-beschwerde-gegen-dfl-auflagen-ein.html |title=RB Leipzig legt erneut Beschwerde ein |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=12 May 2015 |website=t-online.de |location=Darmstadt |publisher=Digital Media Products GmbH |language=de |access-date=30 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=11 May 2015 |title=Jetzt entscheidet der Bayern-Boss |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/lizenz-zoff-35911402.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=30 December 2015}}</ref> Sporting director Ralf Rangnick confirmed that the club was still in talks with the DFL and expressed optimism around the license.<ref name="auto"/> On 15 May 2014, a compromise was announced. The compromise meant that the club had to redesign its crest and ensure that club management was independent from Red Bull GmbH.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=15 May 2014 |title=RB Leipzig erhält Lizenz für zweite Bundesliga |url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/bundesliga/dfl-rb-leipzig-erhaelt-lizenz-fuer-zweite-bundesliga-12941657.html |language=de |newspaper=Frankfurter Allgemeine |location=Frankfurt am Main |publisher=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung GmbH |access-date=30 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=15 May 2014 |title=RB Leipzig erhält Lizenz für 2. Bundesliga |url=http://www.zeit.de/sport/2014-05/rasenballsport-leipzig-bundesliga-dfl |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=30 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=16 May 2014 |title=Lizenz ebnet RB Leipzigs geplanten Weg an die Spitze |url=http://www.sueddeutsche.de/news/sport/fussball-lizenz-ebnet-rb-leipzigs-geplanten-weg-an-die-spitze-dpa.urn-newsml-dpa-com-20090101-140516-99-01799 |language=de |newspaper=Süddeutsche Zeitung |location=München |publisher=Süddeutsche Zeitung Digitale Medien GmbH |access-date=30 December 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023020804/http://www.sueddeutsche.de/news/sport/fussball-lizenz-ebnet-rb-leipzigs-geplanten-weg-an-die-spitze-dpa.urn-newsml-dpa-com-20090101-140516-99-01799 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
[[File:Austria vs. USA 2013-11-19 (118).jpg|thumb|left|Terrence Boyd playing a match for the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] in November 2013]]

The club signed numerous players before the [[2014–15 RB Leipzig season|2014–15 season]], among them [[Rani Khedira]] from [[VfB Stuttgart]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nachrichten |first1=Stuttgarter |title=VfB Stuttgart: Rani Khedira wechselt zu RB Leipzig |url=https://www.stuttgarter-nachrichten.de/inhalt.vfb-stuttgart-rani-khedira-wechselt-zu-rb-leipzig.3ae7701c-6816-4e0c-be4e-dae3529ae94c.html |website=stuttgarter-nachrichten.de |access-date=16 November 2024 |language=de |date=16 June 2014|trans-title=VfB Stuttgart: Rani Khedira is moving to RB Leipzig}}</ref> [[Lukas Klostermann]] from [[VfL Bochum]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Klostermann out for several months with injury |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37489138/rb-leipzig-lukas-klostermann-several-months-injury |publisher=ESPN |access-date=16 November 2024 |language=en |date=14 September 2016}}</ref> [[Marcel Sabitzer]] from [[FC Red Bull Salzburg]], [[Terrence Boyd]] from [[Rapid Wien]] and [[Massimo Bruno]] from [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|RSC Anderlecht]].<ref>{{cite web |title=RB leistet sich heimlich Bruno |url=https://www.kicker.de/rb-leistet-sich-heimlich-bruno-608607/artikel |website=kicker |access-date=16 November 2024 |language=de-DE |date=25 July 2014}}</ref> Several players also left the team. Massimo Bruno and Marcel Sabitzer were immediately transferred on loan to FC Red Bull Salzburg.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kurioser Transfer: Marcel Sabitzer zu Red Bull Salzburg – über Leipzig |url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/marcel-sabitzer-zu-red-bull-salzburg-uber-leipzig-6640660.html |publisher=Der Tagesspiegel |access-date=16 November 2024 |language=de-DE |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241116233727/https://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/marcel-sabitzer-zu-red-bull-salzburg-uber-leipzig-6640660.html|archive-date=16 November 2024|date=30 May 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref> Fabian Bredlow was transferred on loan to [[FC Liefering]], André Luge was transferred on loan to [[SV Elversberg]] and Thiago Rockenbach Silva joined Hertha BSC II as a free agent.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The club spent an estimated sum of approximately 12 million euros on new players during the summer of 2014. The sum was large enough to put the club in 8th place of all clubs in the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga, thus spending more than half of all clubs in the first division.<ref>{{cite news |last=Grimm |first=Anne |date=2 September 2014 |title=RB Leipzig investiert fast 12 Millionen Euro in neue Spieler |url=http://leipzig.sportbuzzer.de/2-bundesliga/artikel/rb-leipzig-investiert-fast-12-millionen-euro-in-neue-spieler/5890/1 |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304050244/http://leipzig.sportbuzzer.de/2-bundesliga/artikel/rb-leipzig-investiert-fast-12-millionen-euro-in-neue-spieler/5890/1 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref>

RB Leipzig played a series of friendly matches during the 2014–15 pre-season. On 18 July 2014, the team defeated [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] 4–2 in front of 35,796 spectators at the Red Bull Arena. The first goal was scored by Terrence Boyd, scoring his second goal in his second match for his new club. Terrence Boyd received the jersey of [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] from Paris Saint-Germain after the match.{{relevance inline|date=January 2024|reason=do players not often swap jerseys at the end of matches? why is this player receiving this other player's jersey – at the end of a friendly match in pre-season – relevant to this football club? possibly in Terrence Boyd's article? but here?}}<ref>{{cite news |last=Gabriel |first=Yvonne |date=18 July 2014 |title=Ärger bei 4:2-Sensations-Sieg gegen Paris Saint-Germain: Leipzig-Stars zoffen sich um Ibrahimovic-Trikot |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/leipzig/rb-leipzig/boyd-klaut-frahn-ibrahimovic-trikot-36878168.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2014/07/18/american-exports-red-bull-leipzigs-terrence-boyd-strikes-again-time-against-paris-st |title=American Exports: Red Bull Leipzig's Terrence Boyd strikes again, this time against Paris St-Germain |last=Seltzer |first=Greg |date=18 July 2014 |website=mlssoccer.com |publisher=Major League Soccer, L.L.C |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref> On 26 July 2014, the team defeated [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] with 2–0 at the [[Stadion der Freundschaft (Gera)|Stadion der Freundschaft]] in [[Gera]]. Both goals were scored by Yussuf Poulsen.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gabriel |first=Yvonne |date=26 July 2014 |title=2:0 im Test gegen Queens Park Rangers: Poulsen schießt die Bullen zum Sieg |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/yussuf-poulsen-schiesst-die-bullen-zum-sieg-gegen-queens-park-rangers-36989492.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref>

The 2014–15 2. Bundesliga season began with 0–0 draw against [[VfR Aalen]] on 2 August 2014, followed up by a couple of wins and another draw.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The first defeat in the league came at the 6th matchday, losing 1–2 against [[1. FC Union Berlin]] at the Red Bull Arena on 21 September 2014.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} After the 7th matchday, the club stood at second place in the league.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} RB Leipzig was drawn against [[SC Paderborn 07|SC Paderborn]] in the first round of the [[2014–15 DFB-Pokal]]. The team won the match 2–1 in extra time at the Red Bull Arena on 16 August 2014. In the second round, the club faced [[FC Erzgebirge Aue]], who they defeated 3–1 in extra time at the Red Bull Arena on 29 October 2015, qualifying for the round of 16 for first time in club history.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=26 October 2014 |title=DFB-Pokal RB Leipzig dreht Spiel: 3:1 gegen Erzgebirge Aue nach Verlängerung |url=http://www.mz-web.de/rb-leipzig/dfb-pokal-rb-leipzig-dreht-spiel--3-1-gegen-erzgebirge-aue-nach-verlaengerung,27404014,28892658.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Mitteldeutsche Zeitung]] |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref> RB Leipzig then released its own club magazine ''Klub'' on 6 October 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dierotenbullen.com/neuigkeiten/Saison_2014_15/KLUB-Magazin-Oktober-November.html |title=KLUB – das neue Vereinsmagazin der Roten Bullen feiert Premiere! |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=n.d. |website=dierotenbullen.com |publisher=RasenBallsport Leipzig GmbH |language=de |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref>

After a run of poor results, the club had dropped down to 7th place by the 13th matchday.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} On 23 November 2014, RB Leipzig defeated [[FC St. Pauli]] 4–1 in front of 38,660 spectators at the Red Bull Arena.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Two goals were scored by Terrence Boyd and the club climbed to 5th place. The success, however, was followed by a draw against [[SV Sandhausen]]. On 7 December 2014, the team met first placed team [[FC Ingolstadt 04|FC Ingolstadt]].{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} RB Leipzig lost 0–1, and the result meant that the club now stood at 8th place.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} RB Leipzig strengthened the team during the winter break by signing [[Omer Damari]] from Austria Wien, [[Emil Forsberg]] from [[Malmö FF]] and players [[Rodnei]] and [[Yordy Reyna]] from FC Red Bull Salzburg. The club spent an estimated sum of 10,7 million euros on new players during the winter break, a sum which covered almost all transfer expenditures during the period for the whole of 2. Bundesliga.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wöckener |first=Lutz |date=19 January 2015 |title=Red-Bull-Millionen verpflichten Leipzig zum Aufstieg |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/article136527814/Red-Bull-Millionen-verpflichten-Leipzig-zum-Aufstieg.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ran.de/fussball/zweite-liga/bildergalerien/transfer-ausgaben-rb-leipzig-fast-gleichauf-mit-borussia-dortmund2 |title=Transfer-Ausgaben: RB Leipzig fast gleichauf mit Borussia Dortmund |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=n.d. |website=ran.de |location=Unterföhring |publisher=ProSiebenSat.1 Digital GmbH |language=de |access-date=21 November 2015 |archive-date=12 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210712104807/https://www.ran.de/fussball/zweite-liga/bildergalerien/transfer-ausgaben-rb-leipzig-fast-gleichauf-mit-borussia-dortmund2 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
[[File:Emil Forsberg - Malmö FF - 2013.jpg|thumb|upright|Emil Forsberg playing a match for Malmö FF against [[AIK Fotboll|AIK]] in June 2013]]

On 6 February 2015, the club lost 2–0 to [[FC Erzgebirge Aue|Erzgebirge Aue]].{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} As a consequence, the club had now played four matches without a win and had lost contact with the top placed teams.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} On the following Tuesday evening, the club summoned Alexander Zorninger to a meeting, and on Tuesday night, the club took the decision to part ways with him after the season.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The decision had been taken by the club management in consultation with Red Bull GmbH owner Dietrich Mateschitz.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The next morning, Alexander Zorniger announced his own decision to leave immediately.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The club received criticism for its decision. Under Alexander Zorniger, the club had risen from the Regionalliga to the 2. Bundesliga. Some media considered the decision to be a merciless one.<ref>{{cite news |last=Armbrecht |first=Anne |date=11 February 2015 |title=Leipziger Logik |url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/alexander-zorniger-und-rb-leipzig-gehen-getrennte-wege-13422357.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Frankfurter Allgemeine]] |location=Frankfurt am Main |publisher=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung GmbH |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=11 February 2015 |title=Trainer Zorniger schmeißt bei RB Leipzig hin |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article137335266/Trainer-Zorniger-schmeisst-bei-RB-Leipzig-hin.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref> Incumbent RB Leipzig U17 coach [[Achim Beierlorzer]] was announced as interim head coach for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kroeme |first=Ullrih |date=12 February 2015 |title=RB-Trainer Beierlorzer: Rangnicks verlängerter Arm |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig-das-ist-interimstrainer-achim-beierlorzer-a-1018146.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |location=Hamburg |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Gabriel |first=Yvonne |date=23 April 2015 |title=Morgen kann Beierlorzer schon besser als Vorgänger Zorniger sein – Wann macht ihn Rangnick zum richtigen Chef? |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/beierlorzer-morgen-schon-besser-als-zorniger-40653728.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref>

On 5 March 2015, RB Leipzig met [[VfL Wolfsburg]] in the third round of the 2014–15 DFB-Pokal. The club was eliminated after being defeated 2–0 at the Red Bull Arena. The match was attended by 43,348 spectators. It was the first time in club history that the stadium had been completely sold out.<ref name="17Malausverkauft">{{cite web |url=http://www.n-tv.de/sport/fussball/Wie-Red-Bull-die-Leipziger-euphorisiert-article14638721.html |title=Bundesliga? "17 Mal ausverkauft!" – Wie Red Bull die Leipziger euphorisiert |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=5 March 2015 |website=n-tv.de |location=Cologne |publisher=n-tv Nachrichtenfernsehen GmbH |language=de |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref> The preferred candidate of sporting director Ralf Rangnick as new head coach from the summer was former [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]] coach [[Thomas Tuchel]], but the negotiations with Tuchel failed.{{vague|date=January 2024}} Another candidate was [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] junior coach [[Sascha Lewandowski]], but he too declined the offer. In May 2015, sporting director Ralf Rangnick was himself announced as new head coach from the summer, with Achim Beierlorzer as his assistant. Ralf Rangnick was planned{{by whom|date=January 2024|reason=who made this plan?}} to serve this double job for one season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport1.de/fussball/2-bundesliga/2015/05/tuchel-und-lewandowski-sagen-rb-leipzig-ab |title=Tuchel und Lewandowski sagen RB Leipzig ab – Rangnick findet nur: Rangnick |last=Winkler |first=Pierre |date=29 May 2015 |website=sport1.de |location=Ismaning |publisher=Sport1 GmbH |language=de |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=29 May 2015 |title=Neuer Leipzig-Trainer Rangnick: Dann mach ich's eben selbst |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/warum-ralf-rangnick-neuer-trainer-von-rb-leipzig-ist-a-1036248.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |location=Hamburg |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref> RB Leipzig finished the [[2014–15 2. Bundesliga|2014–15 2. Bundesliga season]] in fifth place.

Before the [[2015–16 RB Leipzig season|2015–16 season]], RB Leipzig invested further in strengthening the team, signing [[Davie Selke]] from [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]], [[Atınç Nukan]] from [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]], [[Marcel Halstenberg]] from FC St. Pauli and [[Willi Orban]] from [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]]. Selke was signed for an estimated €8 million, Nukan for an estimated €5 million and Halstenberg for an estimated €3 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.t-online.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/id_74785726/2-bundesliga-rb-leipzig-ist-mit-abstand-der-transfer-kroesus-.html |title=Leipzig Transfer-Krösus mit 22,6 Millionen Euro |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=21 July 2015 |website=t-online.de |location=Darmstadt |publisher=Digital Media Products GmbH |language=de |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305185526/http://www.t-online.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/id_74785726/2-bundesliga-rb-leipzig-ist-mit-abstand-der-transfer-kroesus-.html |archive-date=5 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=31 August 2015 |title=Nächster Millionentransfer: RB Leipzig holt St. Paulis Halstenberg |url=http://www.zeit.de/news/2015-08/31/fussball-naechster-millionentransfer-rb-leipzig-holt-st-paulis-halstenberg-31103408 |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> Meanwhile, [[Joshua Kimmich]] was sold to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] and [[Rodnei]] left to join [[TSV 1860 München|1860 Munich]] as free agent. RB Leipzig also made transfers with its unofficial sister club, FC Red Bull Salzburg. As at several times in the past, three players were signed on a free transfer, among them the [[Austria national football team|Austrian national]] [[Stefan Ilsanker (footballer)|Stefan Ilsanker]]. They were joined by Massimo Bruno and Marcel Sabitzer, returning to RB Leipzig from being on loan. These transfers provoked anger among the fans of FC Red Bull Salzburg. For several years, FC Red Bull Salzburg had transferred some of its best players to RB Leipzig.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Fans of FC Red Bull Salzburg were heard singing chants against RB Leipzig during a game in the [[Austrian Cup|ÖFB-Cup]] in April 2015, after Austrian media had reported that Stefan Ilsanker could move to Leipzig during the summer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kurier.at/sport/fussball/zwietracht-in-der-red-bull-familie-salzburg-fans-beschimpfen-rb-leipzig/127.775.092|title=Zwietracht in der Red-Bull-Familie|website=kurier.at|date=29 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=30 April 2015 |title=Red Bull Salzburg Fans singen gegen RB Leipzig |url=http://www.faszination-fankurve.de/index.php?head=Red-Bull-Salzburg-Fans-singen-gegen-RB-Leipzig&folder=sites&site=news_detail&news_id=9669 |language=de |newspaper=Faszination Fankurve |location=Brühl |publisher=Faszination Fankurve, Sole trader: Johannes Mäling |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Fritz |first=Thomas |date=27 June 2015 |title=Wenn Red-Bull-Fans "Scheiß RB Leipzig" singen |url=http://www.zeit.de/sport/2015-06/rb-leipzig-salzburg-spielerwechsel |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref>

The signing of Davie Selke was record breaking, as it made him the most expensive player ever signed in the 2. Bundesliga's history.<ref>{{cite news |last=Nordmann |first=Nils |date=3 March 2016 |title=RB Leipzigs Rekordtransfer versauert auf der Bank |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article152909255/RB-Leipzigs-Rekordtransfer-versauert-auf-der-Bank.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref> In total, the club spent a sum of approximately €18.6 million on new players during the summer of 2015, more than all other clubs in the 2. Bundesliga together.<ref>{{cite news |last=Möthe |first=Alexander |date=24 July 2015 |title=RB Leipzig als Krösus: Die berechenbarste 2. Liga aller Zeiten |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig-als-kroesus-die-berechenbarste-2-liga-aller-zeiten/12103018.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Handelsblatt]] |location=Düsseldorf |publisher=Handelsblatt GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Krause |first=Stefan |date=2 October 2015 |title=Im Winter kein Millionen-Umbau |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/kein-mio-umbau-des-kaders-42859012.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> During the pre-season 2015–16, RB Leipzig defeated [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] 5–4 in [[Bischofshofen]] on 8 July 2015,<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=8 July 2015 |title=RB Leipzig siegt im Test gegen Premier-League-Team Southampton |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/RB-Leipzig-siegt-im-Test-gegen-Premier-League-Team-Southampton |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023011140/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/RB-Leipzig-siegt-im-Test-gegen-Premier-League-Team-Southampton |url-status=dead}}</ref> and [[FC Rubin Kazan|Rubin Kazan]] 1–0 in [[Leogang]] on 12 July 2015.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bohländer |first=Marc |date=12 July 2015 |title=RB Leipzig schlägt Rubin Kasan – Russen sehen zweimal Rot |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/RB-Leipzig-schlaegt-Rubin-Kasan-Russen-sehen-zweimal-Rot |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012902/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/RB-Leipzig-schlaegt-Rubin-Kasan-Russen-sehen-zweimal-Rot |url-status=dead}}</ref> The team then beat [[Hapoel Tel Aviv F.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] 3–0 at the Red Bull Arena on 18 July 2015.<ref>{{cite news |last=Angermann |first=Johannes |date=18 July 2015 |title=RB Leipzig gewinnt Test gegen Hapoel Tel Aviv |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/RB-Leipzig-gewinnt-Test-gegen-Hapoel-Tel-Aviv |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023011008/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/RB-Leipzig-gewinnt-Test-gegen-Hapoel-Tel-Aviv |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The club was drawn against [[VfL Osnabrück]] in the first round of the [[2015–16 DFB-Pokal]]. The match was played at the [[Stadion an der Bremer Brücke|Osnatel-Arena]] in [[Osnabrück]] on 10 August 2015. After Osnabrück scored in the first minute, the home fans celebrated so violently that barriers and safety net partially collapsed and the match had to be interrupted. The match was restarted and Osnabrück led the match into the second half. In the 71st minute, referee Martin Petersen was badly hit in the head by a lighter, thrown from the home stand. The lighter had been thrown after Petersen had tried to resolve an argument between Davie Selke and Osnabrück substitute [[Michael Hohnstedt]], resulting from a controversial situation in the Osnabrück [[penalty area]]. The match was again interrupted, and later cancelled.<ref>{{cite news |last=Frömmert |first=Michael |date=10 August 2015 |title=DFB ermittelt nach Spielabbruch bei RB-Leipzig-Spiel in Osnabrück |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/DFB-ermittelt-nach-Spielabbruch-bei-RB-Leipzig-Spiel-in-Osnabrueck |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012838/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/DFB-ermittelt-nach-Spielabbruch-bei-RB-Leipzig-Spiel-in-Osnabrueck |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=10 August 2015 |title=Pokalspiel zwischen Osnabrück und RB Leipzig abgebrochen |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/article145058215/Pokalspiel-zwischen-Osnabrueck-und-RB-Leipzig-abgebrochen.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> RB Leipzig offered a replay,<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=14 August 2015 |title=Keine Wiederholung: Abgebrochenes Pokalspiel wird für Leipzig gewertet |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/pokalspiel-osnabrueck-gegen-leipzig-wird-nicht-wiederholt-a-1048145.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |location=Hamburg |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> but the DFB decided the match to be counted as lost by Osnabrück 0–2.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/sportgericht-wertet-abgebrochenes-spiel-mit-20-fuer-rb-leipzig-128686/ |title=Sportgericht wertet abgebrochenes Spiel mit 2:0 für RB Leipzig |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=14 August 2015 |website=dfb.de |publisher=Deutscher Fußball-Bund e.V. |location=Frankfurt am Main |language=de|access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> RB Leipzig later decided to waive 20,000 euros of the 50,500 euros VfL Osnabrück owed the club for its share of the revenues from the match. RB Leipzig also allowed the payment of the remaining 30,500 to be postponed until the next year.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=21 November 2015 |title=Leipzig verzichtet zugunsten von Osnabrück auf 20.000 Euro |url=http://www.rp-online.de/sport/fussball/dfb-pokal/rb-leipzig-verzichtet-zugunsten-von-osnabrueck-auf-20000-euro-aid-1.5577010 |language=de |newspaper=RP Online |location=Düsseldorf |publisher=RP Digital GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref>

In the midst of the [[2015 European migrant crisis]], the club, staff, players and fans of RB Leipzig showed support for refugees. In August 2015, RB Leipzig donated €50,000 to the City of Leipzig for its work with helping asylum seekers.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The club also sold 60 containers from its training center, including sanitary facilities, to the city, in order to serve as accommodation for asylum seekers.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The club had originally invested around €500,000 in the containers.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Moreover, the club became patrons of the initiative "Willkommen im Fußball", giving refugee children the opportunity to play football.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=7 August 2015 |title=RB Leipzig unterstützt Flüchtlinge und spendet Geld |url=https://www.welt.de/regionales/sachsen/article144944074/RB-Leipzig-unterstuetzt-Fluechtlinge-und-spendet-Geld.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=7 August 2015 |title="Willkommen im Fußball": RB Leipzig unterstützt Flüchtlingsarbeit in Leipzig mit Geld und Containern |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-unterstuetzt-Fluechtlingsarbeit-in-Leipzig-mit-Geld-und-Containern |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023063036/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-unterstuetzt-Fluechtlingsarbeit-in-Leipzig-mit-Geld-und-Containern |url-status=dead}}</ref> Staff and players of RB Leipzig collected and donated sporting equipment and private clothes to refugees.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Also sporting director and head coach Ralf Rangnick participated in the donation, with personal concern for the commitment, citing his own background as being a child to refugees.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} His parents had met in a refugee camp at [[Glauchau]], his father had fled from [[Königsberg]] and his mother from [[Breslau]].<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=26 August 2015 |title=Spieler von RB Leipzig spenden Kleidung für Flüchtlinge |url=http://www.focus.de/regional/leipzig/fussball-spieler-von-rb-leipzig-spenden-kleidung-fuer-fluechtlinge_id_4905500.html |language=de |newspaper=FOCUS Online |location=München |publisher=FOCUS Magazin Verlag GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=29 August 2015 |title=Spenden aus dem Kleiderschrank: Profis von RB Leipzig helfen Flüchtlingen |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Spenden-aus-dem-Kleiderschrank-Profis-von-RB-Leipzig-helfen-Fluechtlingen |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012851/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Spenden-aus-dem-Kleiderschrank-Profis-von-RB-Leipzig-helfen-Fluechtlingen |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=29 August 2015 |title=RB Leipzig spendet Kleidung für Flüchtlinge |url=https://www.welt.de/regionales/sachsen/article145777873/RB-Leipzig-spendet-Kleidung-fuer-Fluechtlinge.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> By an initiative of fans, RB Leipzig invited refugees on free admission to watch its home match against [[SC Paderborn]] on 11 September 2015.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 September 2015 |title=RB Leipzig lädt Flüchtlinge zum Heimspiel ein |url=http://www.mz-web.de/rb-leipzig/fan-initiative--refugees-welcome--rb-leipzig-laedt-fluechtlinge-zum-heimspiel-ein,27404014,31702734.html |language=de |newspaper=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=ter Vehn |first=Evelyn |date=3 September 2015 |title=RB Leipzig lädt Flüchtlinge zu Paderborn-Spiel ein |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-laedt-Fluechtlinge-zu-Paderborn-Spiel-ein |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012933/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-laedt-Fluechtlinge-zu-Paderborn-Spiel-ein |url-status=dead}}</ref> 450 refugees attended the match, and they were met and accompanied by 200 fans beforehand.<ref>{{cite news |last=Anne |first=Grimm |date=10 September 2015 |title=450 Flüchtlinge besuchen das Heimspiel von RB Leipzig |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/450-Fluechtlinge-besuchen-das-Heimspiel-von-RB-Leipzig |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. RB Leipzig advanced to the second round of the DFB-Pokal, being eliminated after losing 3–0 to a strong playing [[SpVgg Unterhaching]] from the [[Regionalliga Bayern]] at the [[Alpenbauer Sportpark]] on 27 October 2015.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=is the Regionalliga Bayern at the Alpenbauer Sportpark?}}<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=27 October 2015 |title=0:3 in Unterhaching: Leipzig scheitert im Pokal kläglich |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/fussball-dfb-pokal-0-3-in-unterhaching-leipzig-scheitert-im-pokal-klaeglich/12506674.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Handelsblatt]] |location=Düsseldorf |publisher=Handelsblatt GmbH |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123031404/http://www.handelsblatt.com/fussball-dfb-pokal-0-3-in-unterhaching-leipzig-scheitert-im-pokal-klaeglich/12506674.html |archive-date=23 November 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> After defeating SV Sandhausen 2–1 away at the 13th matchday on 1 November 2015, RB Leipzig stood at first place in the league.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=1 November 2015 |title=RB Leipzig gewinnt in Sandhausen und ist Tabellenführer |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/RB-Leipzig-gewinnt-in-Sandhausen-und-ist-Tabellenfuehrer |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 November 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012857/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/Spielberichte/RB-Leipzig-gewinnt-in-Sandhausen-und-ist-Tabellenfuehrer |url-status=dead}}</ref> The position was however quickly lost already at the next matchday,{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='quickly lost already'?}} with the team being surpassed by [[SC Freiburg]] and [[FC St. Pauli]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Krause |first=Stefan |date=9 November 2015 |title=Rangnick sauer auf sich selbst |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/ralf-rangnick/sauer-auf-sich-selbst-43319124.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref> But, following a series of wins, the team returned to the leading position on 13 December 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.t-online.de/sport/id_76393676/2-liga-rb-leipzig-erobert-spitze-freiburg-patzt-in-nuernberg.html |title=RB Leipzig stürmt an die Zweitliga-Spitze |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=13 December 2015 |website=t-online.de |location=Darmstadt |publisher=Digital Media Products GmbH |language=de |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref> RB Leipzig made only few transfers during the winter break. Defender Tim Sebastian, who had been in the team since 2010 and who had once served as captain, left to join SC Paderborn, and midfielder [[Zsolt Kalmár]] left to join [[FSV Frankfurt]] on loan.<ref>{{cite news |last2=Gabriel |first2=Yvonne |last1=Krause |first1=Stefan |date=13 January 2016 |title=Sebastian geht nach Paderborn |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/tim-sebastian-wechselt-zum-sc-paderborn-44140284.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Krause |first=Stefan |date=30 January 2016 |title=Der LEIHse Abschied |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/der-leihse-abschied-44359798.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref>

RB Leipzig held the leading position in the league until the 27th matchday, when it was again lost to SC Freiburg, after the team suffered a 3–1 defeat away against 1.FC Nürnberg on 20 March 2016. The team now stood at second place in the league, only three points ahead of [[1. FC Nürnberg]] in third place.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=20 March 2016 |title=Nürnberg dreht Spitzenspiel gegen RB Leipzig |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/nuernberg-schlaegt-rb-leipzig-bochum-gleicht-in-letzter-minute-aus-a-1083299.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref> RB Leipzig then recorded two straight wins and expanded the distance to six points.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=12 April 2016 |title=Leipzig zieht mit Spitzenreiter Freiburg gleich |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga-leipzig-siegt-gegen-duesseldorf-punktgleich-mit-freiburg-a-1086625.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref> But with only three matches left of the league season, the distance had shrunk to four points.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportschau.de/fussball/bundesliga2/spielbericht-kaiserslautern-fsv-frankfurt-102.html |title=Orbans Platzverweis kostet Leipzig den Sieg |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=25 April 2016 |website=sportschau.de |location=Cologne |publisher=Westdeutscher Rundfunk Köln |language=de |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref> RB Leipzig finally secured a second place in the league and direct promotion to the Bundesliga at the 33rd matchday, after defeating [[Karlsruher SC]] 2–0 in front of 42,559 spectators at the Red Bull Arena on 8 May 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last=Roth |first=Matthias |date=8 May 2016 |title=Aufstieg geschafft: RB Leipzig macht seine Fans glücklich |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Aufstieg-geschafft-RB-Leipzig-macht-seine-Fans-gluecklich |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=28 January 2017 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023062949/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Aufstieg-geschafft-RB-Leipzig-macht-seine-Fans-gluecklich |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="SealPromotion">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=8 May 2016 |title=RB Leipzig seal promotion to first division |url=http://www.dw.com/en/rb-leipzig-seal-promotion-to-first-division/a-19243190 |language=de |publisher=[[Deutsche Welle]] |location=Bonn |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref> The promotion was celebrated together with 20,000 supporters at the Market Square in front of the [[Old Town Hall (Leipzig)|Old Town Hall]] in central Leipzig on 16 May 2016. Leipzig Mayor [[Burkhard Jung]] received the team before the celebration.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=16 May 2016 |title=Aufstiegsfeier Ralf Rangnick: "Heute sind wir alle zusammen Leipzig" |url=http://www.mz-web.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/aufstiegsfeier-ralf-rangnick---heute-sind-wir-alle-zusammen-leipzig--24068118 |language=de |newspaper=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mdr.de/sport/fussball_2bl/rb-leipzig-feiert-aufstieg-100.html |title=RB Leipzig rockt in die Bundesliga |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=17 May 2016 |website=mdr.de |location=Leipzig |publisher=[[Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk]] |language=de |access-date=28 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202032952/http://www.mdr.de/sport/fussball_2bl/rb-leipzig-feiert-aufstieg-100.html |archive-date=2 February 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

At the end of the season, Ralf Rangnick was to resign as head coach,{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='resigned'? or did he announce he would resign? and, then, did he resign? or not resign?}} in order to be able to focus on his job as sporting director. ===2016–present: Bundesliga era===
[[File:20191002 Fußball, Männer, UEFA Champions League, RB Leipzig - Olympique Lyonnais by Stepro StP 0042-2.jpg|thumb|right|RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League]]
RB Leipzig remained undefeated in the first thirteen league matches of the 2016–17 season, breaking a record for the longest undefeated streak of a promoted team to the Bundesliga.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=18 November 2016 |title=RB Leipzig go top and set record by beating Bayer Leverkusen |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/nov/18/bayer-leverkusen-red-bull-leipzig-bundesliga-match-report |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |access-date=20 November 2016}}</ref> The team finished the 11th matchday in first place, and became the first team from the [[new states of Germany|area of former East Germany]] to hold the leading position since the [[1991–92 Bundesliga|1991–92 Bundesliga season]], when [[Hansa Rostock]] stood at first place on 31 August 1991 and held the position for three matchdays, relinquishing it after a loss against FC Ingolstadt.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=20 November 2016 |title=25 Jahre nach Hansa: RB Leipzig ist Bundesliga-Spitze – Bayern angefressen |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/25-Jahre-nach-Hansa-RB-Leipzig-steht-an-der-Bundesliga-Spitze |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-date=27 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171027130943/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/25-Jahre-nach-Hansa-RB-Leipzig-steht-an-der-Bundesliga-Spitze |url-status=dead}}</ref>

RB Leipzig became the first Bundesliga debutant, since [[German reunification]], to qualify for a European tournament, doing so with a 4–0 win against [[SC Freiburg]] on 15 April 2017.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=15 April 2017 |title=RB Leipzig hat europäische Spiele sicher |url=http://www.n-tv.de/sport/fussball/RB-Leipzig-hat-europaeische-Spiele-sicher-article19795217.html |language=de |newspaper=n-tv |location=Cologne |publisher=n-tv Nachrichtenfernsehen GmbH |access-date=15 April 2017}}</ref> They were also the first team from the former East Germany to qualify for a European tournament since 1. FC Union Berlin qualified for the [[2001–02 UEFA Cup]]. Subsequently, Leipzig qualified for the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]] after beating [[Hertha BSC]] 4–1 at the [[Olympiastadion (Berlin)|Olympiastadion]] on 6 May 2017, two days before the anniversary of the club's promotion to Bundesliga.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51475532 |title =RB Leipzig: How did Red Bull build a Champions League side from scratch?|date=18 February 2020|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|access-date=20 February 2020}}</ref>

The following season, Leipzig finished in 6th position and also reached the quarterfinals of the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League]] competition, after being transferred from the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]] group stage, which was finished in 3rd position.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=the club came third in the UEFA Europa League that year? or came third in the Champions League that year?}} On 16 May 2018, [[Ralph Hasenhüttl]] resigned as head coach, after an extension of his contract was denied.{{by whom|date=January 2024}} Before the next season, Rangnick was announced as new coach for one year, to be followed by [[Julian Nagelsmann]] by the beginning of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/ralph-hasenhuettl-rb-leipzig-und-trainer-gehen-offenbar-getrennte-wege-a-1208039.html|title=Hasenhüttl nicht mehr Trainer von RB Leipzig|website=Der Spiegel|publisher=SPIEGEL Gruppe|language=de|date=16 May 2018|access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.welt.de/sport/article179024938/RB-Leipzig-Nachfolge-geloest-Manager-Ralf-Rangnick-wird-Trainer.html|title=Ralf Rangnick wird Trainer bei RB Leipzig|newspaper=Die Welt|language=de|date=9 July 2018|access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.n-tv.de/sport/fussball/Nagelsmann-kehrt-Hoffenheim-den-Ruecken-article20492053.html|title=Nagelsmann kehrt Hoffenheim den Rücken|website=n-tv.de|publisher=Ntv|language=de|date=21 June 2018|access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref>
RB Leipzig finished the [[2018–19 Bundesliga]] season in 3rd position, with a total of 66 points.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} This ensured them qualification in the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League]].{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} In addition, a win against [[Hamburger SV]] on 23 April 2019, RB Leipzig reached the DFB-Pokal final for the first time, where they faced [[Bayern Munich]] on 25 May.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Bayern Munich thrashed RB Leipzig 3–0. On 1 June 2019, Rangnick announced his resignation as sporting director of RB Leipzig after seven years and moved to the Red Bull company as "Head of Sport and Development Soccer". His successor as sporting director was Markus Krösche.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Zelle |first1=Christian |url=https://www1.wdr.de/sport/fussball/erste-bundesliga/sc-paderborn-kroesche-leipzig-100.html|title=Paderborn: Krösche ersetzt Rangnick in Leipzig|website=wdr.de|publisher=WDR|language=de|date=4 June 2019|access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref>
[[File:20180920 Fussball, UEFA Europa League, RB Leipzig - FC Salzburg by Stepro StP 8146.jpg|thumb|left|[[Yussuf Poulsen]] against [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Salzburg]]]]

In the 2019–20 UEFA Champions League, RB Leipzig won their group ahead of [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]], [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] and [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]]. After beating [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] 4–0 on aggregate in the Round of 16,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2020/03/10/football/rb-leipzig-tottenham-champions-league-spt-intl/index.html|title=Thrilling RB Leipzig runs riot to dump Jose Mourinho and Tottenham out of the Champions League|publisher=CNN|date=10 March 2020}}</ref> Leipzig then had a 2–1 win against [[Club Atlético de Madrid|Atlético Madrid]] in the quarter-final, with a late goal of American midfielder [[Tyler Adams]], to reach the semi-final.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53730258 |title=RB Leipzig 2–1 Atlético Madrid |website=BBC Sport |date=13 August 2020}}</ref> But [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] thrashed RB Leipzig 3–0 in the semi-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53759778|title=RB Leipzig 0–3 Paris Saint Germain|work=BBC Sport|date=18 August 2020}}</ref>

Under coach [[Domenico Tedesco]], RB Leipzig reached the semi-finals of the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa League]], in which they were eliminated by [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] 3–2 on aggregate,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dw.com/en/domenico-tedesco-left-to-pick-up-the-pieces-following-rb-leipzigs-latest-low/a-61701358 |title=Domenico Tedesco left to pick up the pieces following RB Leipzig's latest low |website=DW |date=5 May 2022}}</ref> and won their first major title in the [[2022 DFB-Pokal Final|DFB-Pokal Final]] 4–2 on penalties against [[SC Freiburg]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportschau.de/fussball/dfbpokal/pokalfinale-nachdreh-sc-freiburg-rb-leipzig-tedesco-100.html |title=Domenico Tedesco, RB Leipzigs Glücksfall |website=sportschau.de |language=de |date=22 May 2022}}</ref> On 30 July 2022, RB Leipzig faced [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in their first [[2022 DFL-Supercup|DFL Supercup]] at the Red Bull Arena where they lost 5–3.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/supercup/das-spiel/?spieledb_path=%2Fmatches%2F2338381 |title=RB Leipzig 3–5 Bayern München |website=dfb.de |language=de |date=30 July 2022}}</ref> On 7 September 2022, Tedesco was sacked following a 4–1 home defeat against [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] in the opening match of the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=RB Leipzig part company with Domenico Tedesco |url=https://rbleipzig.com/en/news/2022-2023/tedesco-departure/ |access-date=7 September 2022 |website=rbleipzig.com |date=7 September 2022 |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002222410/https://rbleipzig.com/en/news/2022-2023/tedesco-departure/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 3 June 2023, RB Leipzig won their second consecutive [[2022–23 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]] title after a 2–0 win against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] in the final. They also won their maiden [[DFL-Supercup]] on 13 August 2023, beating Bayern Munich 3–0, a revenge for the previous year's Supercup loss.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.redbull.com/int-en/rb-leipzig-win-dfb-cup-2023 |title=Title defended! RB Leipzig win the German Cup in 2–0 Berlin final |publisher=Red Bull |date=5 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report/_/gameId/669439|title=Harry Kane's Bayern Munich debut spoiled by Super Cup loss|date=12 August 2023|work=ESPN|accessdate=16 August 2023}}</ref> On 30 March 2025, [[Marco Rose]] was dismissed as head coach after some poor results in the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.kicker.de/noch-vor-pokal-halbfinale-leipzig-trennt-sich-von-rose-1101936/artikel | title = Noch vor Pokal-Halbfinale: Leipzig trennt sich von Rose | language = de | website = kicker.de | date = 30 March 2025 | access-date = 26 April 2025}}</ref> By the end of the season, RB Leipzig finished seventh in the league, missing out on European competition for the first time since their promotion to Bundesliga in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportschau.de/fussball/bundesliga/leipzig-schafft-europa-quali-nicht,bundesliga-rbl-vfb-100.html |title=Leipzig schafft Europa-Quali nicht |publisher=Sportschau |language=de |date=17 May 2025 }}</ref>

==Colours and crest==
[[File:2020-03-10 Fußball, Männer, UEFA Champions League Achtelfinale, RB Leipzig - Tottenham Hotspur 1DX 3861 by Stepro.jpg|thumb|2020 season kit featuring club's forward [[Timo Werner]]]]
RB Leipzig play in the traditional red and white colours of Red Bull football teams.<ref name="Teufel"/><ref name="Independent1"/> All crests proposed at the club's founding were rejected by the Saxony Football Association (SFV), as they were considered copies of the corporate logo of Red Bull GmbH. The team therefore played its inaugural season in 2009–10 without a crest.<ref name="nehmenAnlauf"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.spox.com/de/sport/fussball/oberliga/0908/News/rb-leipzig-geht-ohne-vereinswappen-in-saison.html |title=RB Leipzig geht ohne Vereinswappen in Saison |last=Gruber |first=Haruka |date=4 August 2009 |website=spox.com |publisher=Perform Media Deutschland GmbH |language=de |access-date=1 April 2016}}</ref> RB Leipzig later proposed a new crest, which was eventually accepted by the SFV in May 2010.<ref name="GegendenGeist">{{cite news |last=Biermann |first=Chrisoph |date=6 April 2012 |title=RB Leipzig: Gegen den Geist der 50+1-Regel |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/red-bull-leipzig-gegen-den-geist-der-50-1-regel-a-824548.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |publisher=SPIEGEL ONLINE GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=1 April 2016}}</ref> The crest was slightly different from the crests used by other Red Bull football teams. The two bulls had been altered in shape and a few strokes added.<ref name="ImSogdesKapitals"/> The crest was used from the 2010–11 Regionalliga season until the end of the 2013–14 3. Liga season. The German Football League (DFL) rejected it however, during the license procedure for the 2014–15 2. Bundesliga season.<ref name="Kicker"/> As part of a compromise with the DFL, the club agreed to redesign its crest and introduced the current{{when|date=January 2024}} crest.<ref name="ReferenceA"/> The current{{when|date=January 2024}} crest is significantly different from the crests used by other Red Bull football teams, although it is identical to the modified crest used by [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]] for international matches and due to [[UEFA]] regulations. The yellow sun has been changed in favor of a football and the initials of "RasenBallsport" have been relocated to the bottom of the crest and are no longer highlighted in red.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wöckener |first=Lutz |date=26 May 2014 |title=Das neue Wappen erinnert an ein Fehler-Suchbild |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article128434259/Das-neue-Wappen-erinnert-an-ein-Fehler-Suchbild.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=1 April 2014}}</ref>
