==Stadium==
{{main|Red Bull Arena (Leipzig)}}
[[File:Leipzig stadium.jpg|thumb|right|The [[Red Bull Arena (Leipzig)|Red Bull Arena]]]]
RB Leipzig played its inaugural season in 2009–10 at the Stadion am Bad in Markranstädt. The stadium held 5,000 seats and was the traditional home ground of SSV Markranstädt. But the plans{{vague|date=January 2024}} were that the first team would quickly move to the far larger Zentralstadion,<ref name="PlantLigaEinstieg"/> hopefully in 2010, after an advance to the Regionalliga.<ref name="NewYorkSalzburg"/><ref name="RiesigeChance"/> Red Bull GmbH reserved the naming right to the stadium at the club's founding, meaning that the name could not be sold to anyone else.<ref name="MischtdieBundesliga"/><ref name="RiesigeChance"/><ref name="AufEroberungsfeldzug"/><ref name="BlühendenFußballLandschaft"/> The company negotiated the acquisition of the naming right during the successful 2009–10 season and the proposed new name was approved by the City of Leipzig on 25 March 2010.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kraske |first=Michael |date=11 March 2010 |title=Blechdosen-Arena |url=http://www.zeit.de/2010/11/S-Leipzig-Zentralstadion |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=21 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=25 March 2010 |title=Stadtrat sagt Ja zur Red-Bull-Arena |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/Regionalsport/Stadtrat-sagt-Ja-zur-Red-Bull-Arena |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=21 March 2010 |archive-date=5 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605114041/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/Regionalsport/Stadtrat-sagt-Ja-zur-Red-Bull-Arena |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://leipzig-seiten.de/index.php/sport/21-deutschland/leipzig/10134-zentralstadion-leipzig-wird-zur-red-bull-arena |title=Zentralstadion Leipzig wird zur Red-Bull-Arena |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=25 March 2010 |website=leipzig-seiten.de |location=Leipzig |publisher=LE-news-NET UG |language=de |access-date=21 March 2016 |archive-date=16 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616185641/http://leipzig-seiten.de/index.php/sport/21-deutschland/leipzig/10134-zentralstadion-leipzig-wird-zur-red-bull-arena |url-status=dead}}</ref> Red Bull GmbH then acquired the naming right and the Zentralstadion was renamed "Red Bull Arena" on 1 July 2010. The contract runs until 2040.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=29 June 2010 |title=Leipziger Zentralstadion heißt jetzt "Red Bull Arena" |url=http://diepresse.com/home/sport/fussball/577632/Leipziger-Zentralstadion-heisst-jetzt-Red-Bull-Arena |language=de |newspaper=[[Die Presse]] |location=Wien |publisher=Die Presse Verlags-Gesellschaft m.b.H. & Co KG |access-date=21 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Krause |first=Stefan |date=1 July 2010 |title=Zentralstadion heißt bis 2040 Red Bull-Arena |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/leipzig/wie-oft-wird-rb-hier-deutscher-meister-13141730.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=21 March 2016}}</ref> The inauguration was held on 24 July 2010, in a friendly match against Schalke 04, in front of 21,566 spectators.<ref name="ArenaEröffnung"/>

Red Bull Arena had a capacity of 44,345 seats during the 2014–15 season. In March 2015, RB Leipzig announced that it was going to invest 5 million euros in a redevelopment of the stadium,<ref>{{cite news |last=Schäfter |first=Guido |date=18 March 2015 |title=Schöner wohnen: RB Leipzig investiert fünf Millionen Euro ins Stadion |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Schoener-wohnen-RB-Leipzig-investiert-fuenf-Millionen-Euro-ins-Stadion2 |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 March 2016 |archive-date=5 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605111439/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Schoener-wohnen-RB-Leipzig-investiert-fuenf-Millionen-Euro-ins-Stadion2 |url-status=dead}}</ref> including an expansion of the VIP area, pressbox and wheelchair spaces. It also included two new larger [[Light-emitting diode|LED]] score boards and refurbished player facilities. The VIP area was expanded from 700 seats to approximately 1400 seats. The capacity of Red Bull Arena was reduced to 42,959 seats before the 2015–16 season, due to redevelopment of various stadium areas.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=8 June 2015 |title=Parkhaus am Sportforum kommt, wenn privater Investor Ja sagt |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Parkhaus-am-Sportforum-kommt-wenn-privater-Investor-Ja-sagt |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 March 2016 |archive-date=24 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324215858/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Parkhaus-am-Sportforum-kommt-wenn-privater-Investor-Ja-sagt |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Gabriel |first=Yvonne |date=August 2015 |title=BILD in der neuen Bullen-Kabine |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/bild-in-der-neuen-bullen-kabine-42037240.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Nößler |first=Robert |date=21 August 2015 |title=Red-Bull-Arena wird kleiner – Rangnick macht RB-Spieler zu Innenausstattern |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Red-Bull-Arena-wird-kleiner-Rangnick-macht-RB-Spieler-zu-Innenausstattern |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 March 2015 |archive-date=24 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150824142423/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Red-Bull-Arena-wird-kleiner-Rangnick-macht-RB-Spieler-zu-Innenausstattern |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Krause |first=Stefan |date=9 September 2015 |title=Bullen machen sich schick für die Bundesliga |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/stadion-umbau-fuenf-mio-42501106.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref>

The Red Bull Arena was an all-seater stadium for a long time.{{vague|date=January 2024}} Home supporters are located in sector B. During the general meeting of the supporters' union in 2014, the assembly made a demand to convert sector B into a standing area.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} However, it was considered impossible{{by whom|date=January 2024}} to convert sector B into a standing area at the time, for structural reasons.<ref name="KeineStehplätze">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=19 November 2014 |title=Keine Stehplätze für RB Leipzig Anhänger |url=http://www.faszination-fankurve.de/index.php?head=Keine-Stehplaetze-fuer-RB-Leipzig-Anhaenger&folder=sites&site=news_detail&news_id=8282 |language=de |newspaper=Faszination Fankurve |location=Brühl |publisher=Faszination Fankurve, Sole trader: Johannes Mäling |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref> Sector B was eventually converted into a standing area in the 2021–22 season.

===Attendances===
The 29 July 2011 first round 3–2 victory over [[VfL Wolfsburg]] was the club's first appearance in the [[2011–12 DFB-Pokal]]; the 31,212 spectators gathered marked a club attendance record for the Red Bull Arena.<ref name="LeipzigschmeißtWolfsburg"/><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=30 July 2011 |title=Daniel Frahn blamiert Wolfsburg bis auf die Knochen |url=http://www.abendblatt.de/sport/fussball/article108066728/Daniel-Frahn-blamiert-Wolfsburg-bis-auf-die-Knochen.html |newspaper=[[Hamburger Abendblatt]] |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeitungsgruppe Hamburg GmbH |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref> The record did not stand long though; on 25 October 2011 Leipzig were defeated 1–0 by [[FC Augsburg]], this second-round game of the DFB-Pokal set a new record attendance of 34,341 spectators.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=25 October 2011 |title=DFB-Pokal Sensationen bleiben aus |url=http://www.express.de/sport/dfb-pokal-sensationen-bleiben-aus-4104052 |language=de |newspaper=[[Express (Cologne newspaper)|Express]] |location=Cologne |publisher=DuMont Rheinland Media24 GmbH |access-date=22 March 2016}}{{Dead link|date=February 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>

The last home game of the [[2013–14 3. Liga|2013–14 3. Liga season]] on 3 May 2014 was a chance for RB Leipzig to secure direct promotion to the [[2. Bundesliga]]; Leipzig romped home emphatically winning 5–1 against [[1. FC Saarbrücken]] in a near-sell out capacity Red Bull Arena, in front of a record 42,713 spectators.<ref name="Durchmarschin2.Fußball"/><ref name="Saarbrücken"/> The 43,348 spectators who watched the third round of the [[2014–15 DFB-Pokal]] against VfL Wolfsburg on 4 March 2015, sold out the Red Bull Arena for the first time, setting the current club record for a match at the Red Bull Arena as of 2016.<ref name="17Malausverkauft"/><ref name="Verein">{{cite web |url=http://www.dierotenbullen.com/verein.html |title=Verein |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=n.d. |website=dierotenbullen.com |location=Leipzig |publisher=RasenballSport Leipzig GmbH |language=de |access-date=31 January 2016}}</ref>

RB Leipzig holds two attendance records. The 2011 [[Saxony Cup]] final against [[Chemnitzer FC]] on 1 June 2011 at the Red Bull Arena was attended by 13,958 spectators. The attendance set a new record for a Saxony Cup final.<ref name="SächsischeZeitung"/><ref name="PackendesFinale"/> The record was broken two years later, again in a final between RB Leipzig and Chemnizer FC. The 2013 Saxony Cup final against Chemnitzer FC on 15 May 2013 at the Red Bull Arena was attended by 16,864 spectators.<ref name="PackendesFinale"/> The second attendance record held by RB Leipzig was set during the 2012–13 season, in the qualification for the 3. Liga. The qualifying match against [[Sportfreunde Lotte]] on 29 May 2013 at the Red Bull Arena was attended by 30,104 spectators. The attendance set a new record for a match in the fourth tier of the [[German football league system]].<ref name="RekordKulisse"/>

RB Leipzig played its hundredth match at the Red Bull Arena on 4 October 2015, against [[1. FC Nürnberg]]. At that point, the club reported a total attendance of 1,464,215 spectators, or an average of 14,643 spectators, for matches at the Red Bull Arena.<ref name="Verein"/>

Their first Bundesliga home match was played on 10 September 2016 versus [[Borussia Dortmund]] in front of 42,558 spectators.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} In their debut season, the team averaged 41,454 spectators, or 97% of the stadium's capacity.

===Expansion===
In October 2014, German media reported that the club wanted to expand the Red Bull Arena to 55,000 seats for future first division Bundesliga play. An expansion to 55,000 seats would make the stadium one of the ten largest football venues in Germany. Who was to finance such an expansion remained unclear. German media considered that a possible option was that Red Bull GmbH buy the stadium to make the investments itself, but it was also considered unlikely{{by whom|date=January 2024}} that the current owner would be prepared to sell the stadium, which had just turned profitable.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=22 October 2014 |title=Bei Aufstieg von RB Leipzig: Red-Bull-Arena wird auf über 55.000 Zuschauer ausgebaut |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Bei-Aufstieg-von-RB-Leipzig-Red-Bull-Arena-wird-auf-ueber-55.000-Zuschauer-ausgebaut |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=30 January 2016 |archive-date=18 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218235429/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Bei-Aufstieg-von-RB-Leipzig-Red-Bull-Arena-wird-auf-ueber-55.000-Zuschauer-ausgebaut |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=28 October 2014 |title=Für die Bundesliga: RB Leipzig plant schon ein größeres Stadion |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article133736134/RB-Leipzig-plant-schon-ein-groesseres-Stadion.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=30 January 2016}}</ref>

The club had previously reserved an area near the [[Bundesautobahn 14|A14 motorway]] north of Leipzig, close to the [[Leipzig/Halle Airport]], which could be used to build a completely new stadium. It could also be used to put pressure on the current owner of the Red Bull Arena to agree to an expansion.{{vague|date=January 2024}} In March 2015, German media reported the club considered building a new stadium on the area north of Leipzig. It could be modeled after the [[Veltins-Arena]] in [[Gelsenkirchen]] or the [[Esprit Arena]] in [[Düsseldorf]], with a significantly larger capacity than Red Bull arena, possibly up to 80,000 seats.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=29 October 2014 |title=Bundesliga-Visionen: RB Leipzig plant ein größeres Stadion |url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/bundesliga-visionen-rb-leipzig-plant-groesseres-stadion-13234217.html |language=de |newspaper=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung |location=Frankfurt am Main |publisher=rankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung GmbH |access-date=30 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=7 March 2015 |title=Leipzig plant größeres Stadion |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/neues-stadion-geplant-40053998.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=30 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Kölmel:Ausbau möglich">{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=5 August 2015 |title=Kölmel: Stadionvertrag mit RB Leipzig läuft bis 2020 – Ausbau möglich |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Koelmel-Stadionvertrag-mit-RB-Leipzig-laeuft-bis-2020-Ausbau-moeglich |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=30 January 2016 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012921/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Koelmel-Stadionvertrag-mit-RB-Leipzig-laeuft-bis-2020-Ausbau-moeglich |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="LeipzigsKassen">{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=6 August 2015 |title=RB Leipzig spült Millionen in Leipzigs Kassen |url=http://www.mz-web.de/rb-leipzig/wirtschaftsfaktor-red-bull-rb-leipzig-spuelt-millionen-in-leipzigs-kassen-,27404014,31403334.html |language=de |newspaper=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=30 January 2016}}</ref>

The current{{when|date=January 2024}} owner of Red Bull Arena, Michael Kölmel, commented on plans to build a new stadium in an interview in August 2015. He pointed out how a new stadium on the outskirts of Leipzig could be detrimental to fan culture, and said that Red Bull Arena could be expanded to 55,000 seats, or even more.<ref name="Kölmel:Ausbau möglich"/>

In October 2015, expansion of the Red Bull Arena was back on the agenda. New plans were made to expand the stadium to 57,000 seats, involving Viennese architect Albert Wimmer. Reconstruction could start over the summer break of 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=8 October 2015 |title=Wiener Architekt legt Hand an: Red-Bull-Arena soll auf 57.000 Plätze erweitert werden |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Wiener-Architekt-legt-Hand-an-Red-Bull-Arena-soll-auf-57.000-Plaetze-erweitert-werden |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=30 January 2016 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012934/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Wiener-Architekt-legt-Hand-an-Red-Bull-Arena-soll-auf-57.000-Plaetze-erweitert-werden |url-status=dead}}</ref> In January 2016, the club decided to put the plans on hold, at least until 2017.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=14 January 2016 |title=RB Leipzig: Stadionausbau liegt auf Eis – Sebastian wechselt nach Paderborn |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-Stadionausbau-liegt-auf-Eis-Sebastian-wechselt-nach-Paderborn |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=30 January 2016 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023063032/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-Stadionausbau-liegt-auf-Eis-Sebastian-wechselt-nach-Paderborn |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In February 2016, German newspaper ''[[Leipziger Volkszeitung]]'' reported that club management again considered the possibility of building a new stadium with a capacity of 80,000 seats north of Leipzig. However, a prerequisite for such a project would be that ticket demand exceed the supply of seats in the Red Bull Arena significantly and sustainably. A move to a new stadium could be possible in 2020,{{according to whom|date=January 2024}} when the club's current{{when|date=January 2024|reason=a current contract that expired in 2020?}} contract to lease the Red Bull Arena expires.{{clarify|date=January 2024|reason=did the contract expire? was the move to a new stadium possible?}}<ref>{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=2 February 2016 |title=Stadion-Neubau steht offenbar doch wieder auf der Agenda von RB Leipzig |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Stadion-Neubau-steht-offenbar-doch-wieder-auf-der-Agenda-von-RB-Leipzig |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=2 February 2016 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012913/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Stadion-Neubau-steht-offenbar-doch-wieder-auf-der-Agenda-von-RB-Leipzig |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In December 2016, RB Leipzig offered that the stadium would be sold by former owner Michael Kölmel to the club to continue the plans from the 2015 agenda. Due to the transfer of the arena into ownership of Red Bull, a new stadium would not be pursued. It was planned, that the stadium would expand to a total of 53,840 seats as of summer 2021, beginning from November 2018, when construction works started. However, the plans were changed during construction and the expansion work was completed in 2021 with a total capacity of 47,069 spectators,{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=47,069 spectators watched the expansion work being completed?}} of which 37,069 can be seated, at national competitions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lvz.de/Sportbuzzer/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-kauft-Red-Bull-Arena-und-will-Stadion-auf-57.000-Plaetze-ausbauen|title=RB Leipzig kauft sich für 70 Millionen Euro die Red-Bull-Arena|website=LVZ – Leipziger Volkszeitung|date=22 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportbuzzer.de/artikel/rb-leipzig-enthullt-plane-fur-ausbau-der-red-bull-arena/|title=SPORTBUZZER enthüllt Pläne für Ausbau der Red-Bull-Arena|website=Sportbuzzer.de|access-date=25 July 2019|archive-date=24 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210724204939/https://www.sportbuzzer.de/artikel/rb-leipzig-enthullt-plane-fur-ausbau-der-red-bull-arena/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Training centre===
In 2010, Red Bull announced its intention to engage long term in Leipzig. In this context the club sought a location for a training centre and a [[Youth system|youth academy]]. Towards the end of the year, the club made concrete plans{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=were the plans really made of concrete?}} to invest 30 million euros in a training centre comprising six pitches, offices and a youth academy. The training center was to be located at Cottaweg, partly on the area of the naturally protected [[riparian forest]] Leipziger Auwald and the site of the traditional fair Leipziger Kleinmesse. The plans met objections and concerns from environmental organizations and from the current{{when|date=January 2024|reason=2010? current?}} users of the area, a Leipzig fairground association and the football club BSV Schönau 1983.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Puppe |first1=Matthias |last2=Schäfer |first2=Guido |date=7 September 2010 |title=Planungen für RB-Trainingszentrum: Hürden am Standort Cottaweg |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Planungen-fuer-RB-Trainingszentrum-Huerden-am-Standort-Cottaweg |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=29 December 2015 |archive-date=15 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115011711/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Planungen-fuer-RB-Trainingszentrum-Huerden-am-Standort-Cottaweg |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.deutschlandfunk.de/steuert-leipzig-auf-den-naechsten-sportpolitischen-skandal.1346.de.html?dram:article_id=196065 |title=Steuert Leipzig auf den nächsten sportpolitischen Skandal zu? |last=Hartmann |first=Grit |date=20 November 2010 |website=deutschlandfunk.de |location=Cologne |publisher=Deutschlandradio |language=de |access-date=29 December 2015}}</ref> After negotiations, the City of Leipzig agreed to the plans on 15 December 2010.<ref>{{cite news |last=ter Vehn |first=Evelyn |date=15 December 2010 |title=Leipzigs Stadtrat stimmt RB-Trainingszentrum am Cottaweg mit großer Mehrheit zu |url=http://www.lvz.de/Leipzig/Lokales/Leipzigs-Stadtrat-stimmt-RB-Trainingszentrum-am-Cottaweg-mit-grosser-Mehrheit-zu |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=29 December 2015 |archive-date=17 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210717105757/https://www.lvz.de/Leipzig/Lokales/Leipzigs-Stadtrat-stimmt-RB-Trainingszentrum-am-Cottaweg-mit-grosser-Mehrheit-zu |url-status=dead}}</ref> RB Leipzig and the city of Leipzig later announced that the club was going to invest in an area of 92,000 square meters.<ref name="Cottaweg2011">{{cite news |last=Puppe |first=Matthias |date=7 January 2011 |title=RB Leipzig startet am Cottaweg in das Unternehmen Fußball-Bundesliga |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/RB-Leipzig-startet-am-Cottaweg-in-das-Unternehmen-Fussball-Bundesliga |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=14 June 2016 |archive-date=15 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115015923/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/RB-Leipzig-startet-am-Cottaweg-in-das-Unternehmen-Fussball-Bundesliga |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The construction was to be carried out in two phases and began in March 2011.<ref name="Verein"/> During the first phase, three natural turf pitches, one artificial turf pitch and an artificial hill for physical exercises were built.<ref>{{cite news |last=Puppe |first=Matthias |date=5 October 2011 |title=Zweiter Bauabschnitt beim Trainingszentrum von RB Leipzig – Knackpunkt Umweltverträglichkeit |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Zweiter-Bauabschnitt-beim-Trainingszentrum-von-RB-Leipzig-Knackpunkt-Umweltvertraeglichkeit |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=29 December 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012909/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Zweiter-Bauabschnitt-beim-Trainingszentrum-von-RB-Leipzig-Knackpunkt-Umweltvertraeglichkeit |url-status=dead}}</ref> All four pitches were installed with floodlights, irrigation system and soil heating. Pitch one was also provided with four 38-meter masts producing HD-compatible lightning for optimal television broadcasts. Locker rooms, sanitary facilities and weight rooms were installed in 60 containers, totaling 720 square meters.<ref>{{cite news |last1=KRAUSE |first1=Stefan |last2=Gabriel |first2=Yvonne |date=12 August 2011 |title=BILD.de erklärt die neue Bullenwiese |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/leipzig/rb-leipzig/bild-erklaert-die-neue-bullenwiese-19351548.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. [[File:Trainingszentrum RB Leipzig.jpg|thumb|right|The RB Leipzig training center at Cottaweg]]

The second phase of construction began in January 2014.<ref name="Verein"/> The plans for the second phase were set to create one of Germany's largest training centers for an estimated cost of 35 million euros.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='one of Germany's largest training centers for an estimated cost of 35 million euros'? a training center for a cost? or did the 'plans for the second phase' cost this?}}<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 December 2015 |title=Bullen dürfen am Cottaweg bauen |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/leipzig/rb-leipzig/rb-leipzig-darf-trainingszentrum-bauen-33651960.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=29 December 2015}}</ref> Involved in the project was the [[Dortmund]] based architect Christoph Helbich, who had previously been involved in the building of a new training center for [[Borussia Dortmund]]. For the second phase, the training center was to be expanded with two pitches, an area for goalkeeping practices and a three-story 13,500 square meters sports complex, meant to offer amenities for all RB Leipzig teams, from the U8 team to the professional team. In addition, pitch one was to be provided with a covered grandstand with at least 1,000 seats, for A- and B-junior matches.<ref name="Cottaweg2011"/><ref name="Cottaweg2013">{{cite news |last=Roth |first=Mathias |date=3 May 2013 |title=Gehobene Ausstattung: RB Leipzig baut bis 2015 neues Trainigszentrum am Cottaweg |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/RB-Archiv/Gehobene-Ausstattung-RB-Leipzig-baut-bis-2015-neues-Trainigszentrum-am-Cottaweg |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. The sports complex was opened in September 2015 and is used by the professional team alongside six junior/youth academy teams, ranging from U14 to the reserve team.<ref name="Verein"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.medicke.de/neubau-red-bull-akademie-in-leipzig-eroeffnet/ |title=Neubau Red Bull-Akademie in Leipzig eröffnet |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 December 2015 |website=medicke.de |location=Glauchau |publisher=Medicke Metallbau GmbH |language=de |access-date=29 December 2015 |archive-date=16 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716005653/https://www.medicke.de/neubau-red-bull-akademie-in-leipzig-eroeffnet/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> The facility includes an 800 square-meter indoor hall, an indoor [[tartan track]] for sprint training, weight rooms, cold chambers, a spa area, medical facilities, and individual relaxation rooms for first-team professional players. The complex also houses a media center, new offices, a [[boarding school]] for 50 youth players and a public café.<ref name="Cottaweg2013"/><ref name="SHA"/><ref name="RasenballerbeziehenTrainingszentrum"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Schober |first=Frank |date=13 October 2015 |title=13.500 Quadratmeter mit allem: Blick ins RB-Heiligtum am Cottaweg |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/13.500-Quadratmeter-mit-allem-Blick-ins-RB-Heiligtum-am-Cottaweg |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=29 December 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012926/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/13.500-Quadratmeter-mit-allem-Blick-ins-RB-Heiligtum-am-Cottaweg |url-status=dead}}</ref> At the time of its construction, the RB Leipzig training center with its sports complex was described by the media and journalists as one of the most modern facilities in Germany.<ref name="SHA"/>

Constructed in the spring of 2016 was a covered grandstand with 1,000 seats, an area for motor skills-training and a parking area.<ref name="Verein"/> The artificial hill for physical exercises, humorously called the "[[Felix Magath]] Memorial Hill",{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='humorously'? why? he is alive (at this time). he appears to have no connection to the club? born in Bavaria? played most of his career in Hamburg? does not look like he managed any team near Leipzig?}}<ref>{{cite news |last=Wiederstein |first=Wolfgang |date=8 November 2014 |title=Leipzig – finanziell wie von einem anderen Stern |url=http://diepresse.com/home/sport/fussball/international/4590193/Leipzig-finanziell-wie-von-einem-anderen-SternLeipzig-finanziell |language=de |newspaper=[[Die Presse]] |location=Wien |publisher=Die Presse Verlags-Gesellschaft m.b.H. & Co KG |access-date=31 January 2016}}</ref> was also reconstructed.<ref name="Verein"/>

The club has already{{when|date=January 2024}} plans for even further expansions of the training centre. The club wants to build an additional pitch to the south of the training centre. Such expansion would require more ground from the Leipziger Kleinmesse, and is therefore met{{when|date=January 2024}} with several objections.{{by whom|date=January 2024}}{{vague|date=January 2024}}<ref>{{cite news |last=Grimm |first=Anne |date=17 April 2015 |title=Erweiterung des RB-Trainingsgeländes – Linke: "Leipzig ist kein Selbstbedienungsladen" |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Erweiterung-des-RB-Trainingsgelaendes-Linke-Leipzig-ist-kein-Selbstbedienungsladen |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=29 December 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012840/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Erweiterung-des-RB-Trainingsgelaendes-Linke-Leipzig-ist-kein-Selbstbedienungsladen |url-status=dead}}</ref> More certain{{according to whom|date=January 2024}} is a future expansion to the north of the training center.<ref name="Kleinmessegelände">{{cite news |last1=Trümper |first1=Erik |last2=Krause |first2=Stefan |date=11 April 2015 |title=RB greift nach dem nächsten Grundstück! |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/leipzig/rb-leipzig/greift-nach-naechstem-grundstueck-40495724.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=29 December 2015}}</ref> This area is used by the football club BSV Schönau 1983 and the tennis club TC Grün-Weiß Leipzig. BSV Schönau 1983 has a contract to lease the area until 2026. The club ceded parts of its grounds to RB Leipzig in 2011. For this, the club received compensation. In total, RB Leipzig spent 900,000 euros for the construction of new grounds for BSC Schönau 1983. The area currently{{when|date=January 2024}} leased by BSV Schönau 1983 is already pledged to RB Leipzig when the lease contract ends in 2026.<ref name="Kleinmessegelände"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=8 August 2015 |title=Goldener Bulle für Leipzig |url=http://www.neues-deutschland.de/artikel/980473.goldener-bulle-fuer-leipzig.html |language=de |newspaper=Neues Deutschland |location=Berlin |publisher=Neues Deutschland Druckerei und Verlag GmbH |access-date=29 December 2015}}</ref> 

At the end of 2025, new offices were built in the city's Cottaweg district for the staff to inhabit, improving from the staff needing to work far apart. The club is described as being hopeful for new beginnings with coaching changes throughout the youth ranks and new infrastructure.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stafford-Bloor |first=Sebastian |date=2026-02-11 |title=RB Leipzig and a sense of new beginnings |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7032967/2026/02/11/rb-leipzig-bundesliga-klopp-diomande/ |access-date=2026-06-03 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==Supporters==
===Fanclubs and minor ultras===
[[File:FC Salzburg gegen RasenBallsport Leipzig (Euroleague Gruppenphase Fünfte Runde) 09.jpg|thumb|right|RB Leipzig supporters]]
RB Leipzig has 68 official fanclubs as of August 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Offizielle Fanclubs (OFC) von RB Leipzig {{!}} Ein Überblick |url=https://rbleipzig.com/fans/fanclubs/unsere-fanclubs/ |access-date=22 August 2023 |website=rbleipzig.com |language=de}}</ref> The first two to become registered as official fanclubs were ''L.E Bulls'' and ''Bulls Club'', both registered in 2009. L.E Bulls is the oldest official fanclub,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dierotenbullen.com/de/fans/fanclubs.html |title=Fanclubs |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |website=dierotenbullen.com |location=Leipzig |publisher=RasenBallsport Leipzig GmbH |language=de |access-date=13 May 2018}}</ref> but Bulls Club claims to be the biggest.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bulls-club.de/fanclub/rb-leipzig-fanclub-bulls-club |title=Willkommen im Bulls Club e.V.! |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |website=bulls-club.de |language=de |access-date=27 July 2015 |archive-date=22 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222195422/http://www.bulls-club.de/fanclub/rb-leipzig-fanclub-bulls-club/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> There are also several non-official fanclubs, such as ''Rasenballisten'' and ''Fraktion Red Pride''. RB Leipzig also has a minor [[ultras]] scene, with groups such as ''Red Aces'' and ''Lecrats''.<ref name="UltrasbeiRBLeipzig">{{cite news |last=Schöler |first=Martin |date=20 November 2012 |title=Ultras bei RB Leipzig: "Nicht in ein Korsett zwängen lassen" |url=http://www.l-iz.de/sport/fussball/2012/11/Ultras-bei-RB-Leipzig-Red-Aces-Rasenballisten-63232 |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Internet Zeitung |location=Leipzig |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Thomas |first=Fritz |date=16 April 2015 |title=Die Red-Bull-Kritiker aus der Red-Bull-Arena |url=http://www.zeit.de/sport/2015-04/rb-leipzig-red-bull-ultras |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> The German newspaper ''[[Mitteldeutsche Zeitung]]'' reported that RB Leipzig had 5,000 organized supporters by March 2016.<ref name="Emanzipieren">{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=10 March 2016 |title=Fanstand im Stadion So emanzipieren sich kritische Fans von RB Leipzig |url=http://www.mz-web.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/fanstand-im-stadion-so-emanzipieren-sich-kritische-fans-von-rb-leipzig-23701090 |language=de |newspaper=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref>

Fan clubs and supporter groups are organized{{by whom|date=January 2024}} into a union called ''Fanverband RB Leipzig Fans'', which was founded in 2013.{{by whom|date=January 2024}}{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} This is an umbrella organization for official fan clubs, unofficial fan clubs and other groups. As of 2016, 25 supporter groups were organized in that union.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Each group in the union is represented by two representatives.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The representatives of the supporter groups meet every four to six weeks.{{where|date=January 2024}} The union also holds a general meeting once per year.{{where|date=January 2024}} Those who are not members of a supporter group are allowed to attend the general meeting.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The union is represented by five to seven "fan representatives", elected every second year.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} A maximum of five "fan representatives" are elected by the representatives of the supporter groups, two additional "fan representatives" are elected by the general assembly.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The "fan representatives" are permitted to speak with club officials to communicate ideas and criticism from the supporter base. In order to divide the work of the "fan representatives", the union has created several working groups.<ref name="KeineStehplätze"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://fanverband-rbl.de/fanverband/ |title=Fanverband |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=n.d. |website=fanverband-rbl.de |location=Leipzig |publisher=Fanverband Leipzig |language=de |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://fanverband-rbl.de/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/satzung-fanverband.pdf |title=Satzung des Fanverbandes von RasenBallsport Leipzig e.V. |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=28 April 2014 |website=fanverband-rbl.de |location=Leipzig |publisher=Fanverband Leipzig |language=de |access-date=22 March 2016 |archive-date=5 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405175431/http://fanverband-rbl.de/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/satzung-fanverband.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref> The first general meeting was held in November 2014, and gathered 350 supporters. Among those present were club officials, such as general manager Ulrich Wolter.<ref name="KeineStehplätze"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Gaengler |first=Rene |date=19 November 2014 |title=Vorstoß von RB-Fans für Stehplätze abgelehnt |url=http://fanzeit.de/historische-fanversammlung/14282 |language=de |newspaper=Fanzeit |location=Bochum |publisher=Fanzeit GmbH |access-date=22 March 2016 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023115643/https://fanzeit.de/historische-fanversammlung/14282 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[File:2022-07-21 Fußball, Männer,Freundschaftsspiel, RB Leipzig - FC Liverpool 1DX 2029 by Stepro.jpg|thumb|right|Bulli, the club [[mascot]]]]
Several German newspapers have noted the emergence of distinctly nonconformist supporter groups at the Red Bull Arena. In January 2012, ''[[Leipziger Internet Zeitung]]'' reported on the appearance of ultra group Red Aces. The group members were said to see themselves as "Rasenballisten" and determined not to leave the supporter base solely to Red Bull GmbH.<ref name="UltrasbeiRBLeipzig"/> In May 2014, ''[[Der Tagesspiegel]]'' reported on supporter group IG Rasenballisten. The group was said to highly value the name "RasenBallsport" and to be committed to give the club an identity beyond that offered by Red Bull GmbH, and instead centered the city of Leipzig.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bardow |first=Dominik |date=15 May 2014 |title=Seele gesucht |url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/rb-leipzig-seele-gesucht/9893978.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Tagesspiegel |publisher=Verlag Der Tagesspiegel GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref> In April 2015, ''[[Die Zeit]]'' reported further on this subject, particularly supporter groups IG Rasenballisten and Lecrats. Their central idea was described as "Rasenballismus", stressing the Leipzig identity and the importance of impassioned fans. Lecrats was described as geared towards the anti-commercial values of [[Ultras|ultra culture]] and as critics of Red Bull GmbH. IG Rasenballisten and the ultra groups were said{{by whom|date=January 2024}} to consciously avoid the reductions that apply to official fanclubs and to reject official club merchandise and the commercial name of the stadium.<ref>{{cite news |last=Fritz |first=Thomas |date=16 April 2016 |title=Die Red-Bull-Kritiker aus der Red-Bull-Arena |url=http://www.zeit.de/sport/2015-04/rb-leipzig-red-bull-ultras |language=de |newspaper=Die Zeit |location=Hamburg |publisher=Zeit Online GmbH |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref> In February 2015, the supporter group IG Rasenballisten became a registered voluntary association. The group had previously functioned as an interest community for other groups and individuals in the Red Bull Arena. The ''[[Mitteldeutsche Zeitung]]'' reported that the group describes itself as uniting fanatical and critical fans of RB Leipzig. Members of Rasenballisten said that the group does not hesitate to criticize Red Bull GmbH, when found necessary, and stated that the identity of a club cannot solely rely on the main sponsor. The group also makes a clear political statement: "Together for Leipzig – Rasenball against Racism", a statement which can be found on scarves sold by the group, and on a banner inside the stadium. RB Leipzig had previously refused to allow supporter groups such as Rasenballisten to sell their own merchandise at the stadium, but after lengthy negotiations,{{vague|date=January 2024}} the club gave permission.<ref name="Emanzipieren"/><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=12 February 2016 |title="Kritische" RB Leipzig Anhänger gründen Verein |url=http://www.faszination-fankurve.de/index.php?head=Kritische-RB-Leipzig-Anhaenger-gruenden-Verein&folder=sites&site=news_detail&news_id=12008 |language=de |newspaper=Faszination Fankurve |location=Brühl |publisher=Faszination Fankurve, Sole trader: Johannes Mäling |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref>

The ultra group Red Aces took position against ''Legida'', the local offshoot of the far-right group ''[[Pegida]]''. In January 2015, the Red Aces penned an open letter to the club, the stadium operator, the Mayor of Leipzig and the citizens of Leipzig asking for support against a planned demonstration by Legida. The demonstration was set to begin near the Red Bull Arena, and the group specifically asked for the stadium lights to be switched off at the time of the demonstration. The stadium operator decided to support the initiative and agreed to switch off the lighting.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Grimm |first1=Anne |last2=Roth |first2=Matthias |date=9 January 2015 |title=Stadion und Arena Leipzig: Wegen Legida geht das Licht aus – Wünsche von RB-Fans erfüllt |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Stadion-und-Arena-Leipzig-Wegen-Legida-geht-das-Licht-aus-Wuensche-von-RB-Fans-erfuellt |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=12 December 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012937/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Stadion-und-Arena-Leipzig-Wegen-Legida-geht-das-Licht-aus-Wuensche-von-RB-Fans-erfuellt |url-status=dead}}</ref> Red Aces had also previously asked the club for permission to display banners against racism and Legida during the last home game of 2014. The club refused to approve the requested banners — according to Red Aces, the club did not want politics in the stadium. Despite the ban, the group displayed a banner directed towards Legida, describing the city of Leipzig as diverse, cosmopolitan and tolerant.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stephan |first=Sören |date=8 January 2015 |title=RB Leipzig-Fanclub "Red Aces" positioniert sich gegen die "LEGIDA"-Demonstration |url=http://fanzeit.de/rb-leipzig-fanclub-red-aces-positioniert-sich-gegen-die-legida-demonstration/16165 |language=de |newspaper=Fanzeit |location=Bochum |publisher=Fanzeit GmbH |access-date=12 December 2015 |archive-date=24 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161024195124/http://fanzeit.de/rb-leipzig-fanclub-red-aces-positioniert-sich-gegen-die-legida-demonstration/16165 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=8 January 2015 |title=RB Leipzig verbietet Antirassismus-Spruchbänder? |url=http://www.faszination-fankurve.de/index.php?head=RB-Leipzig-verbietet-Antirassismus-Spruchbaender&folder=sites&site=news_detail&news_id=8620 |language=de |newspaper=Faszination Fankurve |location=Brühl |publisher=Faszination Fankurve, Sole trader: Johannes Mäling |access-date=12 December 2015}}</ref> In response to the demonstrations by Legida, the anti-racist action group ''Rasenball gegen Rassismus'' was founded by RB Leipzig's supporter groups Red Aces, Lecrats, Rabauken – Block 31, and IG Rasenballisten in January 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.netz-gegen-nazis.de/beitrag/rasenballisten-gegen-rassisten-10150 |title=Rasenballisten gegen Rassisten |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=25 March 2015 |website=netz-gegen-nazis.de |publisher=Amadeu Antonio Stiftung |location=Berlin |language=de |access-date=12 December 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304215848/http://www.netz-gegen-nazis.de/beitrag/rasenballisten-gegen-rassisten-10150 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Before the home match against [[SpVgg Greuther Fürth]] on 3 August 2015, Red Aces again asked for permission to display a banner against Legida, with the text ''Ligaspiel und Legida – der Montag ist zum Kotzen da''. The club again refused to approve the requested banner. During the home match against [[FC St. Pauli]] on 23 August 2015, Red Aces defied the supposed ban on anti-racist banners in the stadium through displaying a banner with a clear anti-Nazi message.<ref>{{cite news |last=Loch |first=René |date=28 August 2015 |title=RB Leipzig: Antirassistische Spruchbänder im Stadion unerwünscht |url=http://www.l-iz.de/sport/fussball/2015/08/rb-leipzig-antirassistische-spruchbaender-im-stadion-unerwuenscht-104687 |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Internet Zeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Mitteldeutsche Online Medien Ltd. |access-date=12 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=28 August 2015 |title=RB Leipzig verbietet erneut antirassistische Plakate |url=http://www.faszination-fankurve.de/index.php?head=RB-Leipzig-verbietet-erneut-antirassistische-Plakate&folder=sites&site=news_detail&news_id=10691 |language=de |newspaper=Faszination Fankurve |location=Brühl |publisher=Faszination Fankurve, Sole trader: Johannes Mäling |access-date=12 December 2015}}</ref> Sporting director [[Ralf Rangnick]] later said that there was no ban against anti-racist messages in the stadium, stating that the banner was prohibited before the home match against SpVgg Greuther Fürth because it contained abusive language, and that the club would agree if someone wanted to display a banner with a message such as "RBL Fans against Racism".<ref>{{cite news |last=Tenbusch |first=Ronald |date=31 August 2015 |title=Sind bei RB Leipzig Antirassismus-Banner verboten |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article145773993/Sind-bei-RB-Leipzig-Antirassismus-Banner-verboten.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=12 December 2015}}</ref>

===Fans at away sides===
RB Leipzig supporters travelled in numbers to the first away match of 2016, against [[FC St. Pauli]] on 12 February 2016. Nearly 2,500 RB Leipzig supporters made their way to the [[Millerntorstadion]] and displayed a red and white flag [[tifo]] at the match start.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=12 February 2016 |title=RB Leipzig verliert auf St. Pauli 0:1 Niederlage am Millerntor |url=http://www.mz-web.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig-verliert-auf-st--pauli-0-1-niederlage-am-millerntor-23551292 |language=de |newspaper=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dierotenbullen.com/neuigkeiten/Saison_2015_16/Spielbericht-Rueckspiel-St.-Pauli.html |title=Auswärtsserie trotz Top-Chancen gerissen! 0:1 am Millerntor! |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=12 February 2016 |website=dierotenbullen.com |location=Leipzig |publisher=RasenballSport Leipzig GmbH |language=de |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref> A higher number of RB Leipzig supporters accompanied the team to [[Nuremberg]] one month later. The away match against [[1. FC Nürnberg]] on 20 March 2016 at the [[Grundig-Stadion]] was attended by 2,800 RB Leipzig supporters, according to club statistics. The number set a new club record for away supporters, which was broken in the first two Bundesliga seasons.<ref name="ReiseRekord">{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=16 March 2016 |title=RB Leipzig so beliebt wie nie – Reise-Rekord zum Nürnberg-Spiel |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-so-beliebt-wie-nie-Reise-Rekord-zum-Nuernberg-Spiel |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=14 June 2016 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012900/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/RB-Leipzig-so-beliebt-wie-nie-Reise-Rekord-zum-Nuernberg-Spiel |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=16 March 2016 |title=Vor dem Spitzenspiel in Nürnberg Fan-Aufmarsch beim RBL-Training |url=http://www.mz-web.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/vor-dem-spitzenspiel-in-nuernberg-fan-aufmarsch-beim-rbl-training-23738698 |language=de |newspaper=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dierotenbullen.com/neuigkeiten/Saison_2015_16/Spielbericht-Rueckspiel-Nuernberg.html |title=Nürnberg entscheidet Top-Spiel mit 3:1 für sich! |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=20 March 2016 |website=dierotenbullen.com |location=Leipzig |publisher=RasenballSport Leipzig GmbH |language=de |access-date=22 March 2016}}</ref> More than 7,000 supporters attended away matches in Dortmund, Munich and Berlin, with a one-year record{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=if the record was only for one year, is it important enough to include here?}} at the away match in Berlin, when 8,500 supporters of RBL gathered to watch their team qualify for the UEFA Champions League. One year later, more than 9,000 fans travelled for the last away game of the 2017–18 season in Berlin.

===''Fanprojekt Leipzig''===
{{relevance inline|date=January 2024|reason=if it is for 'young football fans of different clubs in Leipzig', why is it included in the article for this particular football club? how many of the 4 paragraphs included are necessary here?}}
The organization ''Fanprojekt Leipzig'' was founded in 2011 by initiative of the city of Leipzig and is run by Outlaw gGmbH, full name ''Outlaw gemeinnützige Gesellschaft für Kinder- und Jugendhilfe mbH''.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Outlaw gGmbH is a [[Münster]]-based non-profit company for child and youth welfare.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The basic framework of the Fanprojekt Leipzig was concluded by the City of Leipzig, the Free State of Saxony and the German Football Association (DFB), and the organization receives funding from the City of Leipzig and the DFB.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=18 October 2011 |title=Lösung für Fußball-Fanprojekt in Leipzig – Stadt will für Übergangszeit neue Stelle schaffen |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/Regionalsport/Loesung-fuer-Fussball-Fanprojekt-in-Leipzig-Stadt-will-fuer-Uebergangszeit-neue-Stelle-schaffen |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=5 August 2016 |archive-date=18 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818023014/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/Regionalsport/Loesung-fuer-Fussball-Fanprojekt-in-Leipzig-Stadt-will-fuer-Uebergangszeit-neue-Stelle-schaffen |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Fanprojekt Leipzig is an organization for young football fans of different clubs in Leipzig, and works as an independent institution towards the different clubs.{{relevance inline|date=January 2024|reason=if it is for 'young football fans of different clubs in Leipzig', why is it included in the article for this particular football club?}} The main areas for the organization are promoting a positive supporter culture, violence prevention, help for young supporters in problem situations{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='problem situations'?}} and establishing communication between all parties involved, such as supporters, clubs, police and law enforcement.{{vague|date=January 2024}}{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Fanprojekt Leipzig is part of a network of similar Fanprojekts in numerous German cities. The different Fanprojekts are supported by a national coordination office (KOS).

Fanprojekt Leipzig runs a number of{{quantify|date=January 2024}} centers in Leipzig used for purposes such as recreational activities, content projects, painting and creation of minor choreographies, and as meeting places.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='content projects'? 'recreational activities'? minor choreographies'? what exactly is this?}}{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} For each club, the organization offers a social worker or pedagogue who works exclusively with supporters of that club.{{vague|date=January 2024}}{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The organization carries out a variety of recreational and educational activities, including sporting activities, creative projects, readings and discussions and educational programs.{{vague|date=January 2024}}{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The organization has presence during match days, where it is available for personal contact by supporters, police and law enforcement, with the aim to be able to mediate between the parties and have a de-escalating effect.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.leipzig.de/news/news/zwei-jahre-fussball-fanprojekt/ |title=Zwei Jahre Fußball-Fanprojekt der Outlaw gGmbH in Leipzig |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=18 February 2013 |website=leipzig.de |location=Leipzig |publisher=Stadt Leipzig |language=de |access-date=5 August 2016}}</ref>

RB Leipzig entered a cooperation agreement with Fanprojekt Leipzig in 2013.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The cooperation agreement involves collaboration in eight categories, involving both home and away matches, as well as anti-racism work.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The detailed cooperation agreement was by then a novelty in Germany.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='was by then a novelty in Germany'? 'by then'? and if it was a novelty, how was it a novelty? this is not explained for the reader.}}{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} In addition, the RB Leipzig formed a stadium ban commission, in which Fanprojekt Leipzig provides advice to the club. Fanprojekt Leipzig has also arranged a number of{{quantify|date=January 2024}} events, in which supporters can discuss the development of the supporter scene, and whose results are presented for the club.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='the development of the supporter scene'? 'results are presented to the club'? what results? who presents them?}}<ref name="seine Fans">{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=7 September 2015 |title=RB Leipzig und seine Fans "Verstehen, was in der Kurve läuft" |url=http://www.mz-web.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig-und-seine-fans--verstehen--was-in-der-kurve-laeuft--22560796-seite2 |language=de |newspaper=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=12 June 2016}}</ref>

==Organization and finance==
===Association===
RasenballSport Leipzig e.V is a [[Eingetragener Verein|registered voluntary association]].{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} Its executive body is the ''[[Vorstand]]'', the management board.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The management board is appointed by the ''Ehrenrat'', the honorary board.{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} It is also subordinated to the ''Aufsichtsrat'', the [[supervisory board]].{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} The honorary board is elected directly by club members at the general meeting.

Significant organizational changes were made in 2014, following requirements set up by the German Football League (DFL). One of the requirements was to change the composition of organizational bodies. Both the management board and the honorary board had been composed by either employees or agents of Red Bull.<ref name="l-iz.de">{{cite news |last=Schöler |first=Martin |date=24 April 2014 |title=Zweitliga-Lizenz für RB Leipzig: Mehr Verein, weniger Red Bull |url=http://www.l-iz.de/Sport/Fu%C3%9Fball/2014/04/Zweitliga-Lizenz-RB-Leipzig-mehr-Abstand-zu-Red-Bull-54932.html |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Internet Zeitung |location=Leipzig |access-date=27 July 2015 |archive-date=18 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141018193820/http://www.l-iz.de/Sport/Fu%C3%9Fball/2014/04/Zweitliga-Lizenz-RB-Leipzig-mehr-Abstand-zu-Red-Bull-54932.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="leipzig.sportbuzzer.de"/><ref name="welt.de">{{cite news |last=Wöckener |first=Lutz |date=24 April 2014 |title=RB Leipzig darf nur mit neuem Wappen in Liga zwei |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article127277746/RB-Leipzig-darf-nur-mit-neuem-Wappen-in-Liga-zwei.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> This effectively contradicted fundamental principles of the [[50+1 rule]], as interpreted by the DFL,<ref name="l-iz.de"/> and which aims to forbid the influence of third parties on the sporting decisions of a club.<ref name="Kicker"/> As a part of a compromise with the DFL, the club made a binding declaration that it said was intended to ensure that the management board would be occupied by a majority of persons independent of Red Bull.<ref name="ReferenceA"/>

In addition, a supervisory board was added.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 July 2014 |title=RB Leipzig erfüllt Lizenz-Bedingung |url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/bundesliga/zweite-fussball-bundesliga-rb-leipzig-erfuellt-lizenz-bedingung-13025485.html |language=de |newspaper=Frankfurter Allgemeine |location=Frankfurt am Main |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> The honorary board had performed tasks normally performed by a separate controlling organizational body. These functions were now transferred to a newly created supervisory board, capable of performing these tasks independently. The club decided to transfer the former members of the honorary board to the newly created supervisory board.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schöler |first=Martin |date=4 July 2014 |title=RB Leipzig: Kalmar kommt, Gremien neu strukturiert, Derby gegen Aue unter Flutlicht |url=http://www.l-iz.de/Sport/Fu%C3%9Fball/2014/07/RB-Leipzig-Kalmar-kommt-Gremien-neu-strukturiert-56103.html |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Internet Zeiting |location=Leipzig |access-date=27 July 2015 |archive-date=18 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141018184000/http://www.l-iz.de/Sport/Fu%C3%9Fball/2014/07/RB-Leipzig-Kalmar-kommt-Gremien-neu-strukturiert-56103.html |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 July 2014 |title=RB Leipzig erfüllt Lizenz-Bedingung mit neuer Führungsebene |url=http://www.sz-online.de/nachrichten/rb-leipzig-erfuellt-lizenz-bedingung-mit-neuer-fuehrungsebene--2874415.html |language=de |newspaper=Sächsische Zeitung |location=Leipzig |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref>

The association is responsible for men's junior teams from U8 to U14 and all women's football teams.<ref name="Impressum"/>

====Membership====
Voting membership is severely restricted.<ref name="welt.de"/> In contrast to all other association football clubs in Germany, there is no official way to become a voting member of RasenballSport Leipzig e.V. According to Ulrich Wolter, the club does not aspire towards the high number of members of other clubs. Wolter has also pointed at other clubs, where [[Ultras]] have succeeded in creating structures, and stated that the club absolutely wants to avoid such conditions.<ref>{{cite journal |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=RB-Leipzig-Geschäftsführer Ulrich Wolter: "Wir bauen einen Ost-Leuchtturm" |language=de |journal=Sport Bild |pages=36 |issn=0934-3369 |date=8 May 2013}}</ref>

For the establishment of a registered voluntary association, an association is required by German law<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__56.html |title=Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch (BGB) § 56 Mindestmitgliederzahl des Vereins |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |website=gesetze-im-internet.de |publisher=Bundesministerium der Justiz und für Verbraucherschutz |language=de |access-date=27 July 2015 |quote=Die Eintragung soll nur erfolgen, wenn die Zahl der Mitglieder mindestens sieben beträgt.}}</ref> to have at least seven members. Four years after its founding, the club had only 9 members, all employees of Red Bull.<ref name="ReferenceB"/> By 2014 the registration fee for membership stood at 100 euros<ref name="welt.de"/> and the annual membership fee at 800 euros,<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=26 May 2014 |title=2. Fußball-Bundesliga: RB Leipzig ändert sein Logo |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/2-fussball-bundesliga-rb-leipzig-aendert-sein-logo-a-971793.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> in comparison to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] who, by that time, offered membership at annual fees between 30 and 60 euros.<ref name="Guardian1"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Klinger |first=Nikolaus |date=21 January 2014 |title=RB Leipzig muss um Lizenz zittern |url=http://www.salzburg.com/nachrichten/welt/sport/fussball/sn/artikel/rb-leipzig-muss-um-lizenz-zittern-91242/ |language=de |newspaper=Salzburger Nachrichten |location=Salzburg |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.t-online.de/sport/fussball/id_67485604/rb-leipzig-droht-aerger-mit-der-dfl.html |title=Probleme mit der Lizenz – RB Leipzig droht Ärger mit der DFL |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=20 January 2014 |website=t-online.de |location=Darmstadt |publisher=Digital Media Products GmbH |language=de |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> In addition to this, a person willing to pay the fee could not expect to become a member, since the management board could reject an application without notice.<ref name="Guardian1"/><ref name="ReferenceB">{{cite news |last=Rößner |first=Jörg |date=4 December 2014 |title=Warum RB Leipzig nur neun Mitglieder hat |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article122505625/Warum-RB-Leipzig-nur-neun-Mitglieder-hat.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref>

This restrictive membership policy met criticism,{{from whom?|date=January 2024}} thus one of the original requirements set up by the DFL in order to obtain a license for the 2014–15 2. Bundesliga season was to lower the membership fees and open up the association for new members. The club, in response to this pressure from the DFL, announced changes to the membership in June 2014.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=20 June 2014 |title=Neumitglieder bei RB Leipzig ohne Mitbestimmung |url=http://www.faszination-fankurve.de/index.php?head=Neumitglieder-bei-RB-Leipzig-ohne-Mitbestimmung&folder=sites&site=news_detail&news_id=7226 |language=de |newspaper=Faszination Fankurve |location=Brühl |publisher=Faszination Fankurve, Sole trader: Johannes Mäling |access-date=20 December 2015}}</ref> It then became possible for a person to become an "official supporting member". The annual fee for this type of membership is{{when|date=January 2024}} between 70 and 1000 euros and serves to promote junior football within the club. In return, a "supporting member" receives certain privileges, such as a meeting with the professional team and a fitness session at the Red Bull Arena. "Supporting members" also have the right to attend general meetings, ''although without voting rights''.<ref name="mdr.de">{{cite web |url=http://www.mdr.de/sport/fussball_bl/rb-leipzig-gmbh102.html |title=Ausgliederung – "RB Leipzig aus Grauzone" |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=3 December 2014 |website=mdr.de |language=de |access-date=27 July 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925120627/http://www.mdr.de/sport/fussball_bl/rb-leipzig-gmbh102.html |archive-date=25 September 2015}}</ref> In order to improve participation in the association, "supporting members" are represented by one member in the supervisory board.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schäfer |first=Guido |date=13 January 2015 |title=DFL-Lizenauflagen für RB Leipzig: Aufsichtsrat soll durch Fördermitglied verstärkt werden |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/DFL-Lizenauflagen-fuer-RB-Leipzig-Aufsichtsrat-soll-durch-Foerdermitglied-verstaerkt-werden |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=20 December 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023064549/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/DFL-Lizenauflagen-fuer-RB-Leipzig-Aufsichtsrat-soll-durch-Foerdermitglied-verstaerkt-werden |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===GmbH===
On 2 December 2014, the general meeting of the association voted unanimously for the founding of a spin-off organization in the form of a [[GmbH]]. The decision was taken at an extraordinary meeting. Present were 14 voting members and 40 "supporting members".<ref name="dw.de">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 December 2014 |title=RB Leipzig gründet GmbH |url=http://www.dw.com/de/rb-leipzig-gr%C3%BCndet-gmbh/a-18106715 |language=de |publisher=Deutsche Welle |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> Chairman Oliver Mintzlaff stated that the change was made for the club to be able to step up professionally{{vague|date=January 2024}} and to remain competitive.<ref name="ReferenceC">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 December 2014 |title=RB Leipzigs 14 Mitglieder stimmen für Klub-Umbau |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article134955547/RB-Leipzigs-14-Mitglieder-stimmen-fuer-Klub-Umbau.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 December 2014 |title=2. Fußballbundesliga: RB Leipzig beschließt Ausgliederung der Profiabteilung |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig-gliedert-profiabteilung-aus-a-1006243.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Spiegel |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> The ''RasenballSport Leipzig GmbH'' is responsible for the professional team, the reserve team and men's junior teams from U15 and above.<ref name="Impressum"/><ref name="mdr.de"/><ref name="ReferenceC"/>

As of 2015, Red Bull GmbH is the main shareholder of RasenballSport Leipzig GmbH, holding 99 percent of the shares. The remaining one percent is held by the association. However, as required by the 50 + 1 rule, formal power lies with the association, which holds the majority of votes.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=25 September 2015 |title=RB Leipzig: Das steckt hinter dem Retortenclub |url=http://www.tz.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig-fans-stadion-proteste-roten-bullen-red-bull-3554764.html |language=de |newspaper=tz |location=München |publisher=Zeitungsverlag tz München GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=20 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Wöckener |first=Lutz |date=23 November 2015 |title=Warum RB Leipzig von St. Paulis Plänen profitiert |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/article149166336/Warum-RB-Leipzig-von-St-Paulis-Plaenen-profitiert.html |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=20 December 2015}}</ref>

As of April 2016, the [[general manager]] of RasenballSport Leipzig GmbH was Oliver Mintzlaff.<ref name="Impressum"/>

===Sponsorship===
RB Leipzig's kits were first provided by German sportswear brand [[Adidas]] from the club's founding. In 2014, the club switched to the American sportswear brand [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]], in an agreement that was expected to be in place until at least 2025.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=19 April 2014 |title=Nike wird neuer Ausrüster von RB Leipzig |url=http://leipzig-seiten.de/index.php/sport/32-sport/fussball/14347-nike-wird-neuer-ausruester-von-rb-leipzig |language=de |newspaper=Leipzig-Seiten |location=Leipzig |publisher=LE-news-NET UG |access-date=22 October 2015 |archive-date=16 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716123247/https://leipzig-seiten.de/index.php/sport/32-sport/fussball/14347-nike-wird-neuer-ausruester-von-rb-leipzig |url-status=dead}}</ref> In October 2014, the club also entered into promotional agreements with [[Hugo Boss]], [[Porsche]] as youth sponsor, and [[Volkswagen]] for stadium commercials.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schäfer |first1=Guido |last2=Roth |first2=Matthias |date=1 October 2014 |title=Top-Sponsoren für RB Leipzig: VW und Porsche steigen ein – Weiterer Deal vor Abschluss |url=http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Top-Sponsoren-fuer-RB-Leipzig-VW-und-Porsche-steigen-ein-Weiterer-Deal-vor-Abschluss |language=de |newspaper=Leipziger Volkszeitung |location=Leipzig |publisher=Leipziger Verlags- und Druckereigesellschaft mbH & Co. KG |access-date=22 October 2015 |archive-date=23 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023012915/http://www.lvz.de/Sport/RB-Leipzig/News/Top-Sponsoren-fuer-RB-Leipzig-VW-und-Porsche-steigen-ein-Weiterer-Deal-vor-Abschluss |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 20 May 2016, RB Leipzig extended its contract with [[Ur-Krostitzer|Krostitzer Brauerei]] to be its official beer partner until 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dierotenbullen.com/rbl/neuigkeiten/Saison_2015_16/Vertragsverlaengerung-Ur-Krostitzer.html |title=RB Leipzig & Ur-Krostitzer verlängern Partnerschaft bis 2018! |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=20 May 2016 |website=dierotenbullen.com |location=Leipzig |publisher=RasenballSport Leipzig GmbH |language=de |access-date=22 May 2016}}</ref>

===Joint donation, with Dortmund, Bayern and Leverkusen===
In March 2020, RB Leipzig, Borussia Dortmund, Bayern Munich and Bayer Leverkusen, the four German UEFA Champions League teams for the 2019–20 season, collectively gave €20 million to Bundesliga and [[2. Bundesliga]] teams that were struggling financially during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Veth |first1=Manuel |title=Bundesliga Champions League Starters Donate €20 Million To Help With Coronavirus Crisis |website=[[Forbes]] |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/manuelveth/2020/03/27/bundesliga-champions-league-starters-donate-20m-to-help-with-coronavirus-crisis/ |access-date=10 August 2020}}</ref>

===European competitions===
{{main|RB Leipzig in European football}}

====Overview====
Having finished as runners-up in their [[2016–17 Bundesliga|debut season]] in the German top flight, RB Leipzig gained entry to continental football for the first time, specifically the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]]. RB Leipzig is one of the first clubs to qualify for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] so soon (eight years) after its creation.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='one of the first clubs... so soon...'? not even the first club? and how soon is 'soon' here?}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dw.com/en/rb-leipzig-looking-forward-to-champions-league-debut/a-40469025|title=RB Leipzig looking forward to Champions League debut|publisher=[[Deutsche Welle]]|date=12 September 2017|access-date=1 April 2018}}</ref> The campaign also saw Red Bull Salzburg qualify as [[2016–17 Austrian Football Bundesliga|Austrian champions]]; this raised the issue of a possible conflict of interest between the clubs due to the level of influence exerted by Red Bull over both teams and the close sporting relationship between them in various aspects.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/uefa-rules-threaten-to-disqualify-rb-leipzig-or-red-bull/v0j6kr78ol271fvtzim2p67qm|title=UEFA rules threaten to disqualify RB Leipzig or Red Bull Salzburg from Champions League|website=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=22 February 2017 |access-date=2 September 2018}}</ref><ref name=soul>{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/2567291c-2f89-11e7-9555-23ef563ecf9a|title=Red Bull and the fight for football's soul |work=[[Financial Times]]|date=5 May 2017|access-date=1 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/may/12/red-bull-uefa-multiple-ownership-rules|title=Red Bull will need all its energy to overcome Uefa ownership rules|work=[[The Guardian]]|last=Williams|first=Richard|date=12 May 2017|access-date=1 September 2018}}</ref> After examining the operational structures during June 2017, [[UEFA]] declared themselves satisfied under their regulations that the two clubs (particularly Salzburg) were suitably independent from the Red Bull corporation, and sufficiently distinct from one another, for both be admitted to their competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/rb-leipzig-fc-salzburg-champions-league-clear-red-bull-link-a7799726.html|title=German clubs won't appeal after Uefa clear RB Leipzig and FC Salzburg for Champions League despite Red Bull link|work=[[The Independent]]|date=20 June 2017 |access-date=2 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40348340|title=Champions League: RB Leipzig and Red Bull Salzburg both allowed to compete|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=20 June 2017|access-date=2 September 2018}}</ref>

In the first season following that ruling, both reached the quarter-finals of the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League]] but did not play each other, with RB Leipzig eliminated by [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], who then also knocked out Salzburg in the semi-finals. However, in the [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League|next edition]] of the same competition, RB Leipzig and Red Bull Salzburg were drawn together in [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League group stage#Group B|Group B]] to meet competitively for the first time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dw.com/en/europa-league-draw-leipzig-drawn-with-sister-club-salzburg-frankfurt-have-it-tough/a-45305086|title=Europa League Draw: Leipzig drawn with 'sister' club Salzburg, Frankfurt have it tough|publisher=[[Deutsche Welle]]|date=31 August 2018|access-date=2 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://allinfo.space/2018/08/31/red-bull-clubs-leipzig-encounters-salzburg/|title=Red-Bull-clubs: Leipzig encounters Salzburg|website=Allinfo|date=31 August 2018|access-date=2 September 2018}}</ref> Salzburg won both fixtures between the clubs (3–2 in Germany, 1–0 in Austria),<ref name="RB Leipzig 2–3 Red Bull Salzburg">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45595454|title=RB Leipzig 2–3 Red Bull Salzburg|work=BBC Sport|date=20 September 2018|access-date=15 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dw.com/en/europa-league-rb-leipzig-hanging-by-a-thread-after-salzburg-loss/a-46514308|title=Europa League: RB Leipzig hanging by a thread after Salzburg loss|publisher=[[Deutsche Welle]] |date=29 November 2018|access-date=15 December 2018}}</ref> and also won all their other matches to top the group, while Leipzig failed to progress after dropping further points against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]].<ref name="balls.ie">{{cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/football/watch-unlikely-rosenborg-goal-saved-celtics-blushes-402894|title=Watch: The Unlikely Rosenborg Goal That Saved Celtic's Blushes|website=Balls|date=14 December 2018|access-date=15 December 2018}}</ref>
