==Criticism==
The establishment of RB Leipzig has led to much criticism in Germany, particularly regarding the involvement of Red Bull GmbH and its restrictive membership policy. This has been seen by German football fans as contrary to common practice in the country, where clubs have traditionally relied on voluntary registered associations, with sometimes a very large number of members, and where the 50 + 1 rule has ensured that club members have a formal controlling stake.<ref name="Guardian1"/><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=14 May 2016 |title=Red Bull gives you wingers |url=https://www.economist.com/news/europe/21698690-bundesliga-east-west-tension-very-much-alive-red-bull-gives-you-wingers |newspaper=[[The Economist]] |location=London |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref> RB Leipzig has received criticism relating to perceptions that it was founded as a [[marketing tool]] and that it increased the commercialization of football in Germany.<ref name="DorfvereinFlügel"/><ref name="Guardian1"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Biermann |first=Christoph |date=27 April 2012 |title=Die Dose der Pandora |url=http://www.11freunde.de/artikel/wie-gefaehrlich-ist-rb-leipzig |language=de |newspaper=[[11 Freunde]] |location=Berlin |publisher=11FREUNDE Verlag GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=11 June 2016 |archive-date=7 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180907182945/https://www.11freunde.de/artikel/wie-gefaehrlich-ist-rb-leipzig |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Eskaliert">{{cite news |last=Wöckener |first=Lutz |date=9 March 2015 |title=Protest gegen RB Leipzig und seine Fans eskaliert |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/2-bundesliga/article138219197/Protest-gegen-RB-Leipzig-und-seine-Fans-eskaliert.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=11 June 2016}}</ref><ref name="Wutfans">{{cite news |last=Horeni |first=Michael |date=16 March 2015 |title=Wutfans in der Bundesliga: Der Kampf der Kurven gegen RB Leipzig |url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/bundesliga/wutfans-gegen-rb-leipzig-der-kampf-der-kurven-13483558.html |language=de |newspaper=Frankfurter Allgemeine |location=Frankfurt am Main |publisher=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung GmbH |access-date=11 June 2016}}</ref><ref name="SpültMillionen">{{cite news |last=Kroemer |first=Ullrich |date=6 August 2015 |title=Wirtschaftsfaktor Red Bull RB Leipzig spült Millionen in Leipzigs Kassen |url=http://www.mz-web.de/sport/fussball/wirtschaftsfaktor-red-bull-rb-leipzig-spuelt-millionen-in-leipzigs-kassen--22644604 |language=de |newspaper=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |location=Halle |publisher=Mediengruppe Mitteldeutsche Zeitung GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref> The club has been rejected as a "marketing club", a "commercial club" or a "plastic club".<ref name="Money">{{cite news |last=Homewood |first=Brian |date=4 December 2014 |title=Soccer-More to RB Leipzig than just money, says Rangnick |url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/soccer-germany-leipzig-idUKL3N0TO4ED20141204 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808113038/http://uk.reuters.com/article/soccer-germany-leipzig-idUKL3N0TO4ED20141204 |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 August 2016 |work=[[Reuters]] |location=London |access-date=11 June 2016}}</ref> This criticism has been widespread, and includes people in the management and among coaches and supporters of other clubs.

Supporters of other Leipzig football clubs, such as [[1. FC Lokomotive Leipzig|Lokomotive Leipzig]] and Sachsen Leipzig, protested against the creation of RB Leipzig. They feared a decline of traditional fan culture in Leipzig, and a commercialization of football in the region. After the partnership with [[SSV Markranstädt]] became known, protests immediately appeared in Leipzig suburbs. [[Red Bull]] advertising boards at the Stadion am Bad in [[Markranstädt]] were smeared with graffiti and a weed killer placed on the pitch to purposely ruin it.<ref name="OperationBundesliga"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.t-online.de/sport/fussball/id_19285472/rb-leipzig-im-stadion-am-bad-beginnt-die-zukunft.html |title=RB Leipzig: Im Stadion am Bad beginnt die Zukunft |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2 July 2009 |website=t-online.de |location=Darmstadt |publisher=Digital Media Products GmbH |language=de |access-date=11 June 2016}}</ref> Protests in Leipzig were generally non-violent.<ref name="Independent1"/> Despite RB Leipzig playing its inaugural season in 2009–10 in the same league as Lokomotive Leipzig and Sachsen Leipzig, criticism from these clubs was moderate. Lokomotive Leipzig chairman Steffen Kubald, nevertheless, said that the match against RB Leipzig would for each team be the match of the season, and referred to RB Leipzig as the "[[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] of the Oberliga" (fifth tier of German football).<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=14 June 2009 |title=Perfekt! Lizenz für RB Leipzig |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/erhaelt-lizenz-8689682.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=11 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Knoblach |first=Jochen |date=4 August 2009 |title=Geld schießt keine Tore. Oder doch? Die Firma Red Bull kauft sich bei einer sächsischen Oberligamannschaft ein – und die Konkurrenz ist sauer Zwischen Liebe und Zorn |url=http://www.berliner-zeitung.de/geld-schiesst-keine-tore--oder-doch--die-firma-red-bull-kauft-sich-bei-einer-saechsischen-oberligamannschaft-ein---und-die-konkurrenz-ist-sauer-zwischen-liebe-und-zorn-15191210 |language=de |newspaper=[[Berliner Zeitung]] |location=Berlin |publisher=Berliner Verlag GmbH |access-date=11 June 2016 |archive-date=10 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810035712/http://www.berliner-zeitung.de/geld-schiesst-keine-tore--oder-doch--die-firma-red-bull-kauft-sich-bei-einer-saechsischen-oberligamannschaft-ein---und-die-konkurrenz-ist-sauer-zwischen-liebe-und-zorn-15191210 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The German economist Dr. Tobias Kollman said in 2009 that he saw Red Bull GmbH as a company with clear economic goals for its projects. Consequently, he described RB Leipzig as a "marketing club" and said that it was the first of this kind in Germany. He described the activities of Red Bull GmbH in Leipzig as a "sports political earthquake" in Germany.<ref name="WirtschaftsExperte"/> [[Borussia Dortmund]] chairman Hans-Joachim Watzke and [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] chairman Heribet Bruchhagen, speaking in 2013 of a "clash of culture", warned that clubs backed by major companies or financially strong patrons could pose a threat to the entire Bundesliga. Critics among RB Leipzig's supporters include the supporter group Rasenballisten, which describes itself as uniting critical supporters. According to what the group members have stated, the identity of a club cannot solely rely on its main sponsor; the group has criticized Red Bull GmbH for dominating how the club is represented externally. The group prefers to place emphasis on the  ''RasenBallsport'' part of the club's name, as well as the Leipzig identity.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.turus.net/sport/7336-rb-leipzigs-aufstieg-in-lotte-gedanken-ueber-tradition-und-kommerz.html |title=RB Leipzigs Aufstieg in Lotte: Gedanken über Tradition und Kommerz |last=Kohlhuber |first=Sören |date=5 June 2013 |website=turus.net |location=Hamburg |publisher=Ströer Digital Media GmbH |language=de |access-date=12 June 2016}}</ref>

Representatives of Red Bull GmbH and RB Leipzig have commented in response to criticism. Sporting director Ralf Rangnick referred to the presence of sponsors and investors at other clubs. He rhetorically asked what the difference was between [[Audi AG|Audi]]'s and [[Adidas AG|Adidas]]'s involvement at Bayern Munich, and the commitment of Red Bull GmbH at RB Leipzig. He admitted, though, that there ''was'' a difference: Bayern Munich first had sporting success, and then sponsors and investors showed their interest. However, he claimed that [[VfL Wolfsburg]] and [[Bayer Leverkusen]] were similar to RB Leipzig, and that VfL Wolfsburg became German champions in 2009, to a large extent due to the financial support from [[Volkswagen AG|Volkswagen]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Wöckener |first=Lutz |date=4 June 2013 |title=Ralf Rangnick: So soll der Fußball von Red Bull aussehen |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/article116831557/So-soll-der-Fussball-von-Red-Bull-aussehen.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=12 June 2016}}</ref> Red Bull co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz said in 2009 that the sports commitment of Red Bull GmbH was ''indeed'' different from the sports commitments of other companies. KG |access-date=12 June 2016}}</ref> Red Bull co-founder Mateschitz also explained in 2007 that when the company is involved in sports, it is integrated and takes responsibility for the sports |access-date=12 June 2016 |quote='Wo wir uns sportlich engagieren, sind wir integriert, übernehmen die Verantwortung für die sportliche Leistung und wollen die Identität von Marke und Sport |language=de |newspaper=Goal (website) |location=Munich |publisher=PERFORM Media Deutschland GmbH |access-date=12 June 2016}}</ref> RB Leipzig club CEO Ulrich Wolter, speaking in 2013 about the club's Nachrichtenfernsehen GmbH |access-date=12 June 2016}}</ref>

[[File:Abramovich Chukotka (cropped).jpg|right|thumb|200px|[[Roman Abramovich]], the Russian oligarch, seen here in 2021, has been repeatedly referenced by both critics of RB Leipzig and by people associated with the club, such as [[Red Bull GmbH]] co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz and RB Leipzig club CEO Ulrich Wolter.]]

Both Dietrich Mateschitz and sporting director Ralf Rangnick have made comments on transfer policy. Dietrich Mateschitz commented on the football commitment of Red Bull GmbH in 2007, and said that the company was "not good stars buyers".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Flohr |first1=Sven |last2=Dunkr |first2=Robet |date=29 April 2007 |title=Red-Bull-Chef will deutschem Klub Flügel verleihen |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/article839837/Red-Bull-Chef-will-deutschem-Klub-Fluegel-verleihen.html |language=de |newspaper=Die Welt |location=Berlin |publisher=WeltN24 GmbH |access-date=12 June 2016 |quote=Nein. What we do, we try to do with our brain. Nothing is easier than to take a bag full of money and go shopping. That is stupid, stupid we are not".<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=23 July 2010 |title=Mateschitz degradiert RB Salzburg |url=http://sportnet.at/home/fussball/bundesliga/1358444/Mateschitz-degradiert-RB-Salzburg |language=de |newspaper=Sportnet |location=Wien |publisher=[[Styria Media Group|Styria Medienhaus Sport GmbH & Co KG]] |access-date=12 June 2016 |quote=Ich bin nicht Abramowitsch. Several people have responded to the rejection of RB Leipzig as a "plastic club", which lacks tradition. Sporting director Joachim Krug, speaking in 2009, characterized RB Leipzig as "a newly founded club" with high ambitions.<ref name="DorfvereinFlügel"/> Head coach Tino Vogel said that, at some point, [[Invented tradition|every new tradition begins]].<ref name="OperationBundesliga"/> Supporters of RB Leipzig were noted for displaying banners saying "Let this tradition begin" during the first competitive matches in 2009,<ref>{{cite news |last=Spannagel |first=Lars |date=21 August 2009 |title=Red Bull Leipzig: Frisch aus der Dose |url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/fussball/fussball-red-bull-leipzig-frisch-aus-der-dose/1584264.html |language=de |newspaper=Der Tagesspiegel |publisher=Verlag Der Tagesspiegel GmbH |location=Berlin |access-date=13 June 2016}}</ref> and manager Dieter Gudel said in 2010 that RB Leipzig could well write "Tradition since 2009" on its pennants.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=did it? 'since 2009'? in 2010?}}<ref name="ImSogdesKapitals"/> Dietrich Mateschitz, speaking in 2013, characterized the only difference between RB Leipzig and FC Bayern Munich as one hundred years of tradition, and that in another five hundred years, RB Leipzig would be five hundred years of age and FC Bayern Munich six hundred years of age. By this, he meant that he expected that RB Leipzig would, some day, become a more traditional club than it is now.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schneider |first=Uwe |date=17 July 2013 |title=Red-Bull-Chef Dietrich Mateschitz erklärt: Den FC Bayern und RB Leipzig wird nur das Alter unterscheiden |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG}}</ref>

Sporting director Ralf Rangnick spoke in 2012 of advantages to working in a new club without tradition. RB Leipzig has received praise too, from businesspeople and politicians. He based this on the assumption that young players would eventually stay in the area and, according to Kölmel, that the overall level of football in Leipzig would rise.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pittelkow |first1=Sebastian |last2=Schottner |first2=Dominik |date=22 July 2009 |title=Michael Kölmel über RB Leipzig: "Extrem erfolgsorientiert" |url=http://www.11freunde.de/interview/michael-koelmel-ueber-rb-leipzig |language=de |newspaper=[[11 Freunde]] |location=Berlin |publisher=11FREUNDE Verlag GmbH & Co. Wenn es Lok und Chemie Leipzig nach der Wende nicht geschafft haben, ihre Kraft im Interesse des Fußballs vor Ort zu bündeln – dann gibt es immer einen lachenden Dritten}}</ref> [[Franz Beckenbauer]], speaking in 2015, predicted that RB Leipzig would be dangerous to Bayern Munich in 35 years, if Red Bull GmbH intends to invest for that long a time, and that RB Leipzig was a concept with a future.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=13 June 2015 |title=Franz Beckenbauer: Wird RB Leipzig der neue FC Bayern? |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/franz-beckenbauer/wird-rb-zum-neuen-fc-bayern-41338842.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=Bild |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. VfL Wolfsburg manager [[Klaus Allofs]], speaking in 2016, said that RB Leipzig was a cast of fortune for Leipzig,{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=what is 'a cast of fortune'? or should it be 'cost a fortune'? that RB Leipzig would cost the city of Leipzig a fortune?}} and a good thing for the region and for German football.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=9 February 2016 |title=Wolfsburg-Manager Allofs Red-Bull-Projekt in Leipzig "ist eine gute Sache" |url=http://www.focus.de/sport/fussball/eine-gute-sache-wolfsburg-manager-allofs-verteidigt-red-bull-projekt-in-leipzig_id_5271529.html |language=de |newspaper=FOCUS Online |location=München |publisher=FOCUS Magazin Verlag GmbH |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref>

In interviews published in German newspaper ''Bild'' in 2011, representatives of several Leipzig football clubs spoke of ways they said their clubs had benefited from RB Leipzig's founding. Former Sachsen Leipzig liquidator Heiko Kratz said that, by 2009, the club was no longer able to finance its youth academy, but by selling its A to D junior teams to RB Leipzig, at least they could give the players a future.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason='at least they could give the players a future'? is there anything more specific? or what is the point of this sentence? 'the players'? what players?}} Then President of SSV Markranstädt Holger Nussbaum said the club had used Red Bull Leipzig's financial compensation to have players that it otherwise would not have, and that it was aiming to reach the Regionalliga. Ralph Zahn, then Head of department at ESV Delitzsch, said that the club had used Red Bull Leipzig's financial compensation to build an artificial turf pitch with floodlights for the cost of 250,000 euros.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gabriel |first=Yvonne |date=1 December 2011 |title=Leipziger Klub-Chefs erzählen: Wir haben von den Bullen profitiert |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/leipzig/rb-leipzig/wir-haben-von-den-bullen-profitiert-21308648.bild.html |language=de |newspaper=[[Bild]] |location=Berlin |publisher=BILD GmbH & Co. KG |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref>

According to a survey carried out by the ''Leipziger Volkszeitung'' in 2009, more than 70% of the residents of Leipzig welcomed Red Bull GmhH's investment in local football.<ref name="Teufel"/> The ''Leipziger Volkszeitung'' published results from a study carried out by Intelligence Research in Sponsorshop (Iris) in 2016.<ref name="ReiseRekord"/> According to the study, RB Leipzig then ranked third favourite team in Saxony and Thuringia, only surpassed by Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.<ref name="ReiseRekord"/> RB Leipzig also had an increase in five out of six image values: sympathetic had increased 2.8 percent to 45.1 percent, native had increased 7.2 percent to 40.5 percent, credible had increased 4.8 percent to 43.8 percent, regionally rooted remained at 45.8 percent, ambitious had increased 3.7 percent to 77.5 percent and passionate had increased 5.8 percent to 47 percent.<ref name="ReiseRekord"/> A study carried out by the company Repucom in 2016 showed that RB Leipzig had a nationwide increase of 60 percent in press, radio and television coverage.<ref name="ReiseRekord"/> It also showed that the reports had become more "objective and complex".<ref name="ReiseRekord"/>
